Currently, only 12% of companies have employees familiar with energy simulation tools, with more than half of respondents never using such software in their projects. Recommendations are prioritized in short- and long-term actions aligned with stakeholder responsibilities to create a feasible path to raise architectural energy literacy, integrate energy considerations into design projects, and move toward a built environment that complies with the national building energy code.

title: Linking Process Capability Improvement to Carbon Reduction in SME Die Casting: A Case Study of Aluminum Alloy Components
summary: High shrinkage-related defect rates in aluminum die casting reduce effective production capacity. They also create energy-intensive re-melting loops, which weaken production planning reliability and environmental performance. This study exa
content: High shrinkage-related defect rates in aluminum die casting reduce effective production capacity. They also create energy-intensive re-melting loops, which weaken production planning reliability and environmental performance. This study examines how Green Lean Six Sigma can stabilize a resource-constrained Small and Medium-Sized Enterprise (SME) die-casting process and translate quality improvement into measurable capacity recovery and Scope 2 electricity-related carbon savings. Based on a 10-month case study, the Define–Measure–Analyze–Improve–Control (DMAIC) framework was integrated with factorial ANOVA, the Response Surface Methodology (RSM), one-way analysis of variance (ANOVA) and statistical process control (SPC). These methods supported process parameter identification, operating-window development and shop-floor process stabilization. The analysis identified the filling speed and mold temperature as significant shrinkage drivers, developed a mold temperature control map, and determined the standardized filling speed at 800 mm/s. The intervention reduced the shrinkage defect rate from 7.19% to 1.46%, reduced the overall scrap rate from 7.60% to 2.71%, and improved the overall sigma level from 2.93 to 3.42. This yield improvement generated a 4.89 percentage-point yield-equivalent capacity gain, avoided 4401 kWh of re-melting electricity, reduced Scope 2 emissions by 2.36 t CO2e, and generated gross annualized savings of RMB 249,214 (USD 35,783). Considering a one-time implementation cost of RMB 31,445 (USD 4515), the first-year net saving was RMB 217,769 (USD 31,268). The findings show that accessible statistical process control methods can provide SMEs with a resource-efficient pathway to improve process stability, capacity utilization and electricity-related environmental performance before investing in advanced digital technologies.

title: Theoretical foundations and methodological advancements in geospatial big data analytics and challenges
summary: The rapid development of spatial data and management technologies has led to a paradigm shift from static GIS to dynamic and data-intensive frameworks, known as geospatial big data frameworks. The evolution of big data is driven by the rapi
content: The rapid development of spatial data and management technologies has led to a paradigm shift from static GIS to dynamic and data-intensive frameworks, known as geospatial big data frameworks. The evolution of big data is driven by the rapid expansion and development of the Earth observation system, IoT, mobile based geolocation data. Accordingly, this literature review aims to provide a structured narrative review of existing literature on geospatial big data, its main features, theoretical foundations, and the challenges and opportunities in handling this multidimensional and heterogeneous dataset. To achieve this, existing literature from 2015 to 2026 is considered in this literature review. The literature review covers the main features of geospatial big data through the 5Vs framework, such as volume, velocity, variety, veracity, and value. Furthermore, it highlights the theoretical and methodological foundation of geospatial big data. Since geospatial datasets are increasing in size and heterogeneous, the traditional theoretical foundations need to be extended to incorporate scalability, automation, and data-driven discovery. This resulted in the emergence of a new hybrid scientific paradigm in geospatial data. One of the main advancements of geospatial big data is the emergence of GeoAI, which integrates geospatial data with advanced algorithms such as machine learning and deep learning. This enables automated knowledge discovery and extraction of complex datasets. Furthermore, recent platforms allow high computational power, storage, and analytical tools needed to handle and process large-scale datasets, including cloud computing platforms. However, though advanced computational platforms have emerged, geospatial big data analytics are challenged by data heterogeneity, bias, and ethical issues. The finding highlights the need for an innovative paradigm in geospatial big data analytics that integrates spatial data with AI to enhance robustness and transferability. The review will serve as a bridge to fill the gap between large data availability and knowledge production for solving complex global challenges. By filling the gap between diverse and massive geospatial data with actionable knowledge, the review shows how geospatial big data could serve as an engine for achieving the sustainable development goals (SDGs), such as monitoring environmental change and climate, urban resilience, and planning, where traditional data sources and computational methods failed to address them.

title: CONTRIBUTION OF TREE SPECIES TO CARBON SEQUESTRATION AT THE PELEFORO GON COULIBALY UNIVERSITY SITE IN KORHOGO (NORTHERN CÔTE D’IVOIRE)
source: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
summary: This study forms part of an assessment of the carbon sequestration capacity of tree species in the courtyard of Peleforo Gon Coulibaly University in Korhogo. The aim was to assess the diversity of tree species and the amount of carbon seque
content: This study forms part of an assessment of the carbon sequestration capacity of tree species in the courtyard of Peleforo Gon Coulibaly University in Korhogo. The aim was to assess the diversity of tree species and the amount of carbon sequestered by the trees in the university courtyard, with a view to demonstrating the importance of these plants and encouraging their conservation. Data collection was carried out using a floristic inventory based on transect surveys. The various surveys identified a total of 1,540 trees comprising 59 species, 51 genera and 24 families, with a density of 37 stems per hectare and an estimated species richness of 2 species per hectare. The amount of carbon sequestered was estimated at 132.63 tonnes, representing an average yield of 3.14 t C/ha. This shows that the tree species on the UPGC campus play an important role in conserving biodiversity and combating climate change. These findings now give us an idea of the total amount of carbon sequestered in the UPGC courtyard. To maintain and increase this amount, the tree species on the university campus will need to be protected and further reforestation undertaken in certain areas of the UPGC courtyard.

title: Sectoral green finance thresholds for managing carbon transition risks: an input–output network approach with evidence from Malaysia
summary: Abstract Green finance is an important instrument for supporting low-carbon transitions; however, its effectiveness depends on targeted allocation that balances emission reduction with economic stability. In Malaysia, which has committed to
content: Abstract Green finance is an important instrument for supporting low-carbon transitions; however, its effectiveness depends on targeted allocation that balances emission reduction with economic stability. In Malaysia, which has committed to achieving net-zero emissions by 2050, the sectoral distribution of green finance remains uncertain, particularly given complex inter-industry linkages. This study addresses this issue by developing a sectoral input–output framework to estimate indicative green finance thresholds associated with managing carbon transition risks. The approach integrates carbon intensity (CI) and Hypothetical Extraction Centrality (HEC) to capture environmental exposure and systemic importance across the national production network. The results suggest that implied green finance needs are concentrated in a limited number of sectors. Electrical and optical equipment emerges as a systemically important sector, while electricity, gas, and water supply show high carbon intensity. Additional sectors, including coke, refined petroleum and nuclear fuel, wholesale and retail trade, and basic and fabricated metals, are associated with relatively higher estimated financing levels. In contrast, service-oriented sectors appear to exhibit lower transition risks. Overall, the findings highlight how scenario-based, sector-specific allocation can provide insights into potential pathways for reducing emissions while maintaining macroeconomic stability. However, these estimates are best understood as indicative, model-based benchmarks that reflect the structural assumptions of a static, one-period input–output framework. The study offers a scalable analytical approach that may help inform green finance discussions in Malaysia and other emerging economies.

title: 13 CO 2 pulse labelling reveals species-specific alterations in carbon allocation and volatile organic compound emissions under heat stress
summary: Temperate forests increasingly face extreme air temperature, but plant physiological responses, particularly alterations in carbon allocation or protection via volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, remain poorly understood. We pulse-la
content: Temperate forests increasingly face extreme air temperature, but plant physiological responses, particularly alterations in carbon allocation or protection via volatile organic compound (VOC) emissions, remain poorly understood. We pulse-labelled well-watered saplings of Fagus sylvatica and Pseudotsuga menziesii in a controlled heat stress experiment with 13 CO 2 to quantify heat-induced shifts in CO 2 , VOC and C pool exchange, specifically analyzing compound-specific δ 13 C of terpenoids, water-soluble organic matter (WSOM) and dark respiration. Under heat stress, up to 50% of fresh assimilates were directed to maintenance respiration and 1-2% to VOC emissions, while net assimilation and water use efficiency decreased by 50-75% in both species. Heat directly affected metabolic processes and reduced turnover rates of fresh assimilates in F. sylvatica , but accelerated them in P. menziesii . Strong 13 C labelling of some compounds, particularly acyclic ones, suggested increased de novo synthesis of specific terpenoids for heat stress protection. By tracing the fate of recently assimilated 13 CO 2 we demonstrate that heat stress reduces net carbon uptake and water use efficiency, disrupts turnover of C pools and increases carbon loss via respiration and de novo synthesis of specific VOCs, potentially diminishing net carbon uptake of forests under future heat extremes.

title: Can digital transformation and foreign direct investment enhance environmental quality? Evidence from selected developing countries
source: VNU JOURNAL OF ECONOMICS AND BUSINESS
summary: Developing countries are heavily reliant on foreign direct investment (FDI) and digital transformation to sustain economic growth and improve productivity. However, these growth drivers may also intensify environmental pressure when they ar
content: Developing countries are heavily reliant on foreign direct investment (FDI) and digital transformation to sustain economic growth and improve productivity. However, these growth drivers may also intensify environmental pressure when they are supported by fossil-fuel-based energy systems. Consequently, the literature on the FDI-CO2 emissions remain inconclusive which necessitates further evidence. By employing an annual panel of 28 developing countries over the period 2000-2022, this study aims to comprehensively evaluate the main factors driving or mitigating CO2 emissions. Empirical results show that energy consumption is the most consistent driver of CO2 emissions. Meanwhile, FDI and digital transformation show positive but statistically insignificant effects in the baseline model, suggesting that their environmental impacts are contextdependent rather than uniform. Moreover, the robustness analysis indicates that renewable energy is negatively associated with CO2 emissions. Overall, the findings suggest that developing countries should place energy transition at the centre of sustainable development strategies. In particular, policymakers should improve energy efficiency, expand renewable energy, attract cleaner FDI and align digital transformation with low-carbon energy planning.

title: Strategic mineral competition and democratic governance in Africa
summary: Abstract African countries have become focal points of a new round of competition among global powers to access key minerals required for an emerging green transition, as well as for advanced digital infrastructure and modern weaponry. In a
content: Abstract African countries have become focal points of a new round of competition among global powers to access key minerals required for an emerging green transition, as well as for advanced digital infrastructure and modern weaponry. In addition to their relatively high level of reserves of such minerals, which include cobalt, lithium, graphite and several types of rare earths, Africa is also home to many of the world’s most important deposits. These mineral riches present, however, a contradictory situation: on one hand, they represent the critical resources needed to achieve a low-carbon future; but on the other hand, these same resources are often extracted under circumstances that contribute to weak or non-existent democratic institutions and support the type of dependency relationships characteristic of the colonial period. This article examines how the competition for control of strategic minerals in Africa impacts domestic governance arrangements and security frameworks. In particular, it examines whether this competition supports or undermines democratic space in African countries through content reviews of official government reports, international treaties or accords, speeches delivered by senior government officials and structured observations. Based on its findings, the project argues that the competition for control of strategic minerals has had an adverse effect on democracy in Africa. Specifically, the project finds that this competition has empowered executives at the expense of parliamentarians and independent judiciaries; has encouraged executive branches to limit parliamentary oversight and judicial review of executive actions related to extraction activities; has allowed governments to expand their authority over regions where extractive activities take place securitize extraction; and has reduced opportunities for citizens to participate in decision-making processes regarding extractive activities. The paper further finds that, because major global actors prioritize securing their supply chains for strategic minerals and positioning themselves geopolitically relative to competitors over holding foreign governments accountable for adhering to democratic norms and standards, there exist significant perverse incentives for governments of African countries to sacrifice democratic principles and procedures to secure foreign investment and cooperation on national security issues. The results contradict liberal theories’ assumption that economic interdependence is likely to lead to better governed countries. The project instead shows that international competition for natural resources can lead to the embedding of anti-democratic governance practices into the national security architecture of states. Finally, the project finds that without developing regional approaches to governing strategic minerals, the probability that illiberal security regimes will develop across sub-Saharan Africa will increase while prospects for democrati

title: Performance of Recycled Concrete Aggregate and Reclaimed Asphalt Pavement in Concrete: A Systematic Review of Mechanical, Physical, and Durability Characteristics
summary: The increasing generation of construction and demolition waste, along with the depletion of natural aggregates, has driven growing interest in recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) and reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) as sustainable alternative
content: The increasing generation of construction and demolition waste, along with the depletion of natural aggregates, has driven growing interest in recycled concrete aggregate (RCA) and reclaimed asphalt pavement (RAP) as sustainable alternatives in concrete production. However, a direct and systematic comparison between the two materials remains limited. This review addresses this gap by applying PRISMA guidelines to analyze 82 peer-reviewed studies published between 2010 and 2026. Both materials are evaluated across three key domains: physical properties, mechanical performance, and microstructural characteristics. The findings indicate that RCA can reduce compressive strength by up to 26%, mainly due to the presence of porous adhered mortar and a complex interfacial transition zone (ITZ). In contrast, RAP weakens bonding with cement paste because of its hydrophobic bituminous coating, leading to adhesive failure at the mortar asphalt interface. Despite these limitations, RCA and RAP exhibit distinct behaviors in terms of shear capacity, ductility, energy absorption, and durability. Enhancement techniques such as surface treatment, carbonation, supplementary cementitious materials, and fiber reinforcement show potential in improving performance. Additionally, life cycle and economic analyses reveal that RAP can reduce total costs and carbon emissions when efficiently processed. This study provides a unified comparative framework to support sustainable material selection and design optimization.

title: Political gatekeeping and digital innovation in sustainable public procurement
summary: Governments are expanding sustainable public procurement to advance climate and social objectives. Integrating sustainability criteria alongside traditional purchasing requirements, however, increases decision complexity and creates persist
content: Governments are expanding sustainable public procurement to advance climate and social objectives. Integrating sustainability criteria alongside traditional purchasing requirements, however, increases decision complexity and creates persistent implementation barriers. Although digital tools can help manage this complexity, their adoption remains limited. This study draws on interviews with procurement technology developers and state and local officials in Europe and the United States to examine both the supply and demand sides of technology adoption for sustainable procurement. The findings identify four interrelated factors shaping uptake: political support, organizational capacity, internal processes, and technology framing. While prior research conceptualizes these factors as analytically distinct and co-equal drivers of adoption, the results suggest a hierarchical interpretation in which political support appears to play an important gatekeeping role. Across both leading and emergent governments, adoption remains limited despite substantial variation in resources, organizational structures, and technology framing. This finding provides empirical leverage and challenges the assumption that adoption drivers operate as parallel, co-equal factors. Political support appears to facilitate access to resources, legitimize process change, and reduce perceived risk, thereby shaping the extent to which organizational and technological factors contribute to adoption. The study advances a more politically grounded theory of technology adoption and develops five propositions that redirect research toward the institutional and political preconditions required to scale digital innovation in sustainable public procurement.

title: Lakes Amplify Carbon Emissions Relative to Downstream Export in Aquatic Networks
summary: Abstract Inland waters emit and export large quantities of carbon (C), and the balance between emission and export determines the role of inland waters in the global C cycle. Modeling studies of stream‐lake networks suggest that C emission‐
content: Abstract Inland waters emit and export large quantities of carbon (C), and the balance between emission and export determines the role of inland waters in the global C cycle. Modeling studies of stream‐lake networks suggest that C emission‐to‐export ratios (emission:export) are higher in lake‐rich networks with longer network residence times (NRT), yet empirical evidence supporting these patterns remains limited. We sampled 362 stream segments and 42 lakes across 32 nested arctic stream‐lake networks, repeated across four seasons with contrasting environmental conditions. The data show that lake‐rich networks have much longer NRT and higher C emission:export regardless of environmental conditions, while overall C emission:export increased during warmer low‐flow periods. Our findings stress the importance of accounting for lakes within stream networks and simultaneously quantifying multiple C fates when assessing the role of inland waters in the C cycle.

title: Location decision factors in food processing and how they can inform a just protein transition
summary: Producers of alternative proteins must carefully consider facility location if they are to achieve commercial success and drive positive impact for environment and society. This review provides insight into the most important factors that i
content: Producers of alternative proteins must carefully consider facility location if they are to achieve commercial success and drive positive impact for environment and society. This review provides insight into the most important factors that influence this decision. Sixteen studies that used expert elicitation, binomial regression or literature to identify key factors were gathered using a systematic PRISMA approach. The findings suggest that producers currently heavily prioritize economic factors, with product and supplier market access, labor cost and proximity to an agglomeration forming the four top factors identified, aligning with clear objectives to reduce cost and increase returns. Just one study mentioned an environmental factor and one mentioned a social factor. For a protein transition to be just, this economic focus must be expanded. Future work is needed to bridge knowledge gaps around the requirements of alternative protein producers to inform and incentivise responsible decision making.

title: Simulasi Investasi IPP PLTS 10 MWp Di Kabupaten Sambas Provinsi Kalimantan Barat
summary: Penelitian bertujuan untuk menganalisis kelayakan teknis, kelayakan finansial, efisiensi, dan sustainability energi pada proyek investasi IPP PLTS 10 MWp di Kabupaten Sambas, Kalimantan Barat. Pendekatan yang digunakan melibatkan ketersedia
content: Penelitian bertujuan untuk menganalisis kelayakan teknis, kelayakan finansial, efisiensi, dan sustainability energi pada proyek investasi IPP PLTS 10 MWp di Kabupaten Sambas, Kalimantan Barat. Pendekatan yang digunakan melibatkan ketersediaan irradiasi matahari sebagai acuan kelayakan teknis, pendekatan time value of money sebagai acuan kelayakan finansial dengan metode NPV, IRR, MIRR, PBP, Discounted PBP, BCR/PI yang diterapkan pada dua skenario yakni, skenario pendanaan capital perusahaan (100% equity) dan skenario loan (70% loan : 30% equity), serta pendekatan EROI dan NEA dalam analisis efisiensi dan sustainability energi. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan proyek layak secara teknis dengan GHI 1684,2 kWh/m²/tahun yang menghasilkan specific production PV 1337,8 kWh/kWp/tahun dengan PR 79% sesuai dengan ketentuan IEC 61724. Pada analisis kelayakan finansial, didapatkan skenario loan menunjukkan rasio pengembalian investasi yang lebih baik dengan NPV Proyek 1.431.115.665, IRR Proyek 10,24%, MIRR Proyek 10,05%, PBP Proyek 7 tahun, Discounted PBP 23 tahun, dan nilai BCR/PI Proyek 1,01. Analisis efisiensi dan sustainability proyek menghasilkan EROI 9.50 dan NEA 1,220,398,551.71 MJ yang merepresentasikan tercapainya efisiensi dan sustainability pada proyek.

title: Influence of Sustainability Marketing Practices on Brand Loyalty of Consumer Goods in Delta State, Nigeria
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: This study investigated the influence of sustainability marketing practices on consumer brand loyalty of household products in Delta State, Nigeria. The specific objectives were to investigate the influence of ecofriendly advertising, Corpo
content: This study investigated the influence of sustainability marketing practices on consumer brand loyalty of household products in Delta State, Nigeria. The specific objectives were to investigate the influence of ecofriendly advertising, Corporate Social Responsibility activities, and ecofriendly product packaging on consumer brand loyalty of household products in Delta State. The study adopted a descriptive research design using a survey research method. The population of the study comprised the consumers of household products in Delta State. The sample size was 382 consumers which was derived using the Cochran (1963) formula. A structured questionnaire was used as an instrument of data collection for the study. Findings of the study indicated that ecofriendly advertising, CSR activities, and ecofriendly product packaging positively influence consumer brand loyalty of household products in Delta State. Therefore, the study concludes that sustainability marketing practices have significant influence on consumer brand loyalty of household products in Delta State, and recommended that business owners should pay attention to eco friendliness when mapping out advertising and product labeling strategies

title: The Civic Argument Literacy Test (CALT) – Foundations and Development
summary: Abstract The Civic Argument Literacy Test (CALT) is a new instrument for measuring how individuals recognise, interpret, and evaluate arguments in civic discourse. This research essay sets out the conceptual and theoretical foundations of t
content: Abstract The Civic Argument Literacy Test (CALT) is a new instrument for measuring how individuals recognise, interpret, and evaluate arguments in civic discourse. This research essay sets out the conceptual and theoretical foundations of the CALT and, as its central contribution, the design principles underlying its ten diagnostic parts. After defining argument literacy as a civic competence and locating the construct within rhetorical theory, argumentation studies, and the new literacy studies tradition, we describe how each dimension is operationalised as a concrete task, and how this relates to existing operationalisations in psychological and pedagogical research studies. We further describe the deliberate move from fully authentic to semi-authentic civic materials, and the iterative shaping of the ten-part structure across two pilot studies and a validation study. A cross-linguistic survey of argumentation, rhetoric, and critical-thinking textbooks provides content-validity evidence: the components the CALT operationalises recur as chapter-level topics in independently authored works from distinct academic traditions. The CALT translates concepts from rhetorical and argumentation theory – enthymemes, argument schemes, rhetorical proofs, visual argument, fallacy recognition – into scalable tasks embedded in semi-authentic public discourse, intended for upper secondary and undergraduate populations. The validation study provides evidence ( N = 178, UK adults aged 18–25) that the CALT has good reliability as a total-score measure, and we discuss its dimensionality and discriminant validity. By bridging argumentation theory with empirical assessment, the CALT contributes to experimental argumentation research, offering a diagnostic tool for studying how citizens process arguments across contexts and populations.

title: A Critical Assessment of the Dynamic Interrelationships Between Poverty, Unemployment and Economic Growth in Nigeria
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: This study investigates the dynamic interrelationships between poverty, unemployment, and economic growth in Nigeria from 1980 to 2023. Utilizing a comprehensive econometric approach, including unit root and cointegration tests, and an erro
content: This study investigates the dynamic interrelationships between poverty, unemployment, and economic growth in Nigeria from 1980 to 2023. Utilizing a comprehensive econometric approach, including unit root and cointegration tests, and an error correction mechanism (ECM), the research examines how poverty and unemployment influence economic growth and how these variables interact in both the short run and long run. The findings reveal that, in the long-run equilibrium there is relationship between poverty, unemployment, and economic growth. In the short run, the findings reveal that poverty and unemployment have negative and significant impact on economic growth in Nigeria. The study concludes that while poverty reduction is crucial, it must be coupled with strategic interventions in unemployment to foster sustained economic growth. The study therefore recommends that government and private sector collaboration should focus on developing industries with high employment potential and investing in vocational training and skills development to match the needs of the labour market.

title: A detailed processing route and electrochemical validation of fuel-electrode supported planar solid oxide cells toward scalable manufacturing
source: Boletín de la Sociedad Española de Cerámica y Vidrio
summary: Planar fuel electrode supported 5 cm × 5 cm solid oxide cells (SOCs) were manufactured by conventional methods such as tape-casting, lamination and screen printing. The chosen materials were a Ni–8% mol Y 2 O 3 -stabilized ZrO 2 (Ni-YSZ) ce
content: Planar fuel electrode supported 5 cm × 5 cm solid oxide cells (SOCs) were manufactured by conventional methods such as tape-casting, lamination and screen printing. The chosen materials were a Ni–8% mol Y 2 O 3 -stabilized ZrO 2 (Ni-YSZ) cermet as fuel electrode, YSZ as electrolyte and lanthanum strontium manganite (LSM)-YSZ or lanthanum strontium cobalt ferrite (LSCF)-gadolinium-doped ceria (GDC) composites as air electrode, including in this later case a GDC barrier layer. Electrochemical characterization and scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis validated the proposed manufacturing methods and allowed a comparison of SOCs performances at several gas concentrations and temperatures. As a reference, EIS measurements at 750 °C with 100% O 2 and 50% H 2 O resulted in polarization resistances of 0.24 Ω cm 2 for the LSCF-GDC cell and 0.60 Ω cm 2 for the LSM-YSZ cell, while the achieved current densities at 1.3 V were 0.56 and 0.40 A/cm 2 , respectively.

title: The Legal Construction of Carbon Benefit Sharing for Customary Law Communities Following Minister of Forestry Regulation No. 6 of 2026
summary: This study analyzes the legal status of customary law communities and carbon benefit sharing under Presidential Regulation No. 110 of 2025 and Minister of Forestry Regulation No. 6 of 2026. It employs normative legal research using statutor
content: This study analyzes the legal status of customary law communities and carbon benefit sharing under Presidential Regulation No. 110 of 2025 and Minister of Forestry Regulation No. 6 of 2026. It employs normative legal research using statutory, conceptual, and case approaches. The findings show that customary law communities holding a formal determination of customary forest status are recognized as Business Actors in carbon trading, although such access operates through conditional inclusion because it depends on the formal designation of customary forests. Rights over customary forests also do not automatically confer ownership of Carbon Units. With respect to benefit sharing, the regulatory framework addresses Padiatapa, benefit-sharing agreements, reporting, evaluation, and grievance mechanisms, but does not yet establish substantive parameters for assessing fairness. This study proposes a rights-and-contribution-based carbon benefit-sharing framework built on four parameters: recognition, consent, contribution, and distribution.

title: Heated tobacco product aerosol exposure induces lung inflammation associated with altered miR-96-5p and FoxO3a expression in mice
summary: Heated tobacco products (HTPs) have recently become increasingly popular among smokers, mainly in Europe and the Western Pacific region, based on the argument that they are healthier alternatives to conventional cigarettes. However, scienti
content: Heated tobacco products (HTPs) have recently become increasingly popular among smokers, mainly in Europe and the Western Pacific region, based on the argument that they are healthier alternatives to conventional cigarettes. However, scientific evidence in support of this argument is insufficient. The aim of the present study was to determine the effects of exposure to HTPs aerosol on the lungs of mice. 10-week-old wild-type male mice (C57BL6/JJcl) were exposed to (low- and high-dose) HTPs aerosol. After two months of exposure, bronchoalveolar lavage fluid (BALF) was collected, then the lungs were dissected and processed for histological evaluation. Inflammation was evaluated by a semiquantitative scoring system. We also determined the expression levels of key inflammation-related mRNAs and aryl hydrocarbon receptor (AhR)-regulated microRNAs. Expression levels of proteins targeted by the microRNAs with altered expression are further measured. HTPs aerosol exposure significantly increased the perivascular inflammation score and the expression of the pro-inflammatory cytokine IL-6, while IL-1β numerically increased and IL-10, an anti-inflammatory cytokine, numerically decreased with increasing doses. The exposure also significantly downregulated the expression of miR-96-5p among AhR-regulated microRNAs and upregulated the expression of its target protein, forkhead box O3a (FoxO3a). HTPs aerosol exposure induced lung inflammation associated with altered expression of miR-96-5p and FoxO3a in mice.

title: The impact of working onboard ships on individual metabolic profiles: Comparing pre-embarkation and post-embarkation testing among Filipino seafarers
summary: BACKGROUND: Filipino seafarers comprise nearly one-third of the global maritime workforce and face oc-cupational exposures that may elevate cardiometabolic risk. Prolonged deployments marked by irregular schedules, limited physical activity
content: BACKGROUND: Filipino seafarers comprise nearly one-third of the global maritime workforce and face oc-cupational exposures that may elevate cardiometabolic risk. Prolonged deployments marked by irregular schedules, limited physical activity, and constrained dietary diversity can influence metabolic regulation. The objective was to examine pre- to post-embarkation changes in metabolic parameters among Filipino seafarers and identify demographic and occupational predictors of these changes. MATERIAL AND METHODS: A retrospective paired analysis of 402 male seafarers was conducted using pre- and post-embarkation medical records. Continuous and categorical parameters were assessed using paired t-tests and McNemar's tests. A repeated-measures ANOVA, adjusted for age and work location, evaluated within-person changes, while generalized estimating equations identified predictors of metabolic outcomes. RESULTS: Significant increases were observed in body mass index (BMI) (26.30 → 26.66 kg/m2; p < 0.001), fasting blood sugar (FBS) (5.13 → 5.28 mmol/L; p < 0.001), impaired fasting glucose (2.2% → 4.5%; p = = 0.035), and hyperuricemia (13.2% → 18.4%; p = 0.034). Serum glutamic-pyruvic transaminase (SGPT) decreased (40.07 → 33.27 U/L; p < 0.001), accompanied by a decline in the prevalence of elevated SGPT (35.3% → 20.4%; p < 0.001). All lipid fractions, creatinine, metabolic syndrome, dyslipidemia, and anemia remained stable. In adjusted models, only SGPT (F (1,397) = 4.63; p = 0.032) and triglycerides (F (1,397) = = 6.082; p = 0.014) showed significant time effects. Generalized estimating equations (GEE) models identified post-embarkation timing as a predictor of impaired fasting glucose [odds ratio (OR) 2.08; p = 0.036], hyperu-ricemia (OR = 1.49; p = 0.036), and reduced odds of elevated SGPT (OR = 0.48; p < 0.001). Engine department assignment (OR = 1.93; p = 0.009) and older age (OR = 1.019; p = 0.037) independently predicted elevated SGPT. CONCLUSIONS: Seafaring deployment is associated with selective metabolic perturbations, particularly affecting glu-cose, uric acid, and hepatic enzyme regulation. These findings highlight occupation as a social determinant of health and emphasize the need for proactive, department-specific metabolic monitoring and shipboard health programs.

title: Two-dimensional Mo2B2Tx MBenes for selective sensing of disease-associated VOCs in cardiovascular diagnostics
summary: Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of global mortality, driving the need for non-invasive early detection methods. Analysis of specific volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath, such as acetone, hexane, hexanal, isoprene,
content: Cardiovascular disease is a leading cause of global mortality, driving the need for non-invasive early detection methods. Analysis of specific volatile organic compounds (VOCs) in exhaled breath, such as acetone, hexane, hexanal, isoprene, and pentane, offers a promising diagnostic pathway. However, the selective detection of these low-concentration VOC biomarkers remains a significant challenge. This study employs a combination of theoretical approaches, such as density functional theory (DFT), STM-based tunnelling model aligned with the Tersoff-Hamann approximation, and thermodynamic analysis via the Langmuir adsorption model, to assess the sensing capabilities of two-dimensional (2D) MBenes (Mo 2 B 2 T x ) monolayers toward the targeted VOCs. The results reveal that VOCs interact with the Mo 2 B 2 T x (T x = H, O, F) surface, exhibiting adsorption energies ranging from −0.18 eV to −1.00 eV, which vary with the VOC type and surface termination. This interaction alters the work function of Mo 2 B 2 T x , with sensitivity values ranging from approximately 5% to over 25%. Considerable changes in the electronic properties of Mo 2 B 2 T x are observed upon the adsorption of VOCs, which are studied through density of states, electrostatic potential, and work function analysis. Recovery times vary widely from 10 −9 s to 10 2 s at 300 K, depending on adsorption strength and surface termination, with only weakly adsorbed species exhibiting ultrafast desorption. Thermodynamic analysis using Langmuir isotherms confirmed large surface coverage of the VOCs at parts-per-million (ppm) concentrations. STM-based I-V simulations show strong VOC in Mo 2 B 2 T x , with acetone producing a clear tunnelling response, while hexane shows minimal interaction. Furthermore, the Mo 2 B 2 T x , particularly Mo 2 B 2 F 2 , retained adequate adsorption for hexanal in the presence of interfering air gases (CO 2 , NO 2 , H 2 O) and in an aqueous medium, as studied through a solvation model, providing preliminary evidence of selectivity under selected interfering gases. The results establish Mo 2 B 2 T x as a promising platform for developing high-performance nanosensors for the detection of specific VOCs related to cardiovascular disease.

title: Climate Change, Information Warfare and Regional Security in the Niger Delta: The Role of Diplomacy, Intelligence and Media
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: Climate change has emerged as one of the most significant non-traditional security threats confronting the global community in the twenty-first century. Beyond environmental degradation, climate change has intensified displacement, poverty,
content: Climate change has emerged as one of the most significant non-traditional security threats confronting the global community in the twenty-first century. Beyond environmental degradation, climate change has intensified displacement, poverty, food insecurity, migration, violent conflicts, and economic instability in many vulnerable regions of the world. In the Niger Delta region of Nigeria, climate change intersects with oil pollution, weak environmental governance, unemployment, social inequality, and insecurity to create complex threats to peace and sustainable development. Copious literature search shows that very limited studies have been conducted on the relationship between climate change, regional security, information warfare and climate disasters in the Niger Delta. This paper examines the relationship between climate change, regional security, and information warfare in the Niger Delta region and determine how flooding, sea level rise, coastal erosion, resource depletion, and environmental degradation continue to undermine social stability. In this study we reviewed over thirty scholarly publications, technical reports, and conference papers and carried out content analysis. Information manipulation, disinformation, governance failures, and propaganda inflame communal tensions and weaken trust in institutions; climate disaster vulnerability has triggered mass displacement, competition over scarce resources and escalating tensions in fragile communities in the Niger Delta region. Effective climate resilience in the Niger Delta requires integrated approaches involving diplomacy, intelligence, media engagement, community participation, and collaborative truth mechanisms. It concludes that climate security and information integrity must become central pillars of sustainable peace building and regional development in Nigeria and across Africa.

title: Dominant-learner adaptive mixing for concrete compressive strength prediction
summary: Accurate prediction of concrete compressive strength is essential for mixture design, quality control, and the broader use of supplementary cementitious materials in low-carbon construction. Fly ash concrete is particularly challenging to m
content: Accurate prediction of concrete compressive strength is essential for mixture design, quality control, and the broader use of supplementary cementitious materials in low-carbon construction. Fly ash concrete is particularly challenging to model because its strength development is affected by nonlinear interactions among binder composition, water–binder relationships, admixture dosage, and material characteristics. To address this problem, this study proposes a Dominant Learner with Adaptive Mixing (DLAM) framework for data-driven strength prediction. DLAM uses inner cross-validation to identify the most reliable learner from a pool of machine learning models and introduces a validation-controlled Ridge calibration step to exploit complementary information among candidate predictions. The calibration branch is adopted only when it improves the inner-validation root mean squared error (RMSE), thereby reducing the risk of unnecessary model combination and performance degradation. The framework is evaluated using a leakage-free repeated outer/inner validation protocol on a fly ash concrete dataset and is further examined on an independent public concrete strength dataset. DLAM is compared with individual learners, adaptive model-averaging baselines, and Stacking. The results show that DLAM achieves the lowest mean RMSE among the focused comparators on both datasets, with a clear improvement on the external dataset and a more modest gain on the fly ash dataset. These findings demonstrate that validation-controlled calibration provides a transparent and robust way to enhance machine-learning-based concrete strength prediction, especially when different learners capture complementary aspects of the mixture–strength relationship.

title: Astragaloside IV attenuates H₂O₂-induced oxidative stress and ferroptosis-like injury in HBZY-1 mesangial cells via the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway
summary: Ferroptosis has recently been demonstrated to play a critical role in the initiation and progression of diabetic nephropathy (DN). Emerging evidence indicates that ferroptosis is tightly regulated by the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway. Astraga
content: Ferroptosis has recently been demonstrated to play a critical role in the initiation and progression of diabetic nephropathy (DN). Emerging evidence indicates that ferroptosis is tightly regulated by the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway. Astragaloside IV (As-IV) exhibits potent antioxidant effects in various disease models. However, whether As-IV inhibits ferroptosis by modulating the Nrf2/HO-1 pathway remains unclear. An in vitro model of oxidative stress-induced ferroptosis-like injury was established by exposing HBZY-1 mesangial cells to H₂O₂ (400 µmol/L) for 4 h. Intracellular ferrous ion (Fe²⁺) levels were measured using a specific fluorescent probe. The expression of ferroptosis-related proteins was detected by Western blotting. Reactive oxygen species (ROS) production was assessed by flow cytometry. Superoxide dismutase (SOD) activity and malondialdehyde (MDA) content were determined using commercial assay kits. The expression levels of Nrf2/HO-1 pathway-related proteins were detected by Western blotting. H₂O₂ significantly increased ROS levels and MDA content, decreased SOD activity, downregulated the expression of Nrf2, HO-1, GPX4, and NQO1, and induced changes in iron metabolism and lipid peroxidation consistent with ferroptosis. As-IV attenuated H₂O₂-induced oxidative stress and ferroptosis-like changes in vitro. Further mechanistic investigation revealed that the Nrf2 inhibitor all-trans retinoic acid (ATRA) reversed the aforementioned effects of As-IV, suggesting that As-IV acts through activation of the Nrf2/HO-1 signaling pathway. The results from the present study suggest that As-IV inhibits ferroptosis, at least in part, through activation of the Nrf2 pathway, with HO-1 identified as a potential key downstream mediator.

title: Land use and land cover change driven by Rohingya refugee settlements in Bangladesh derived from satellite observations using geospatial techniques
summary: The increasing number of Rohingya camps with forced migration from Arakan State over a short period of time has resulted in the limit of attaining environmental landscape. The research study aims to analyze the environmental impact due to t
content: The increasing number of Rohingya camps with forced migration from Arakan State over a short period of time has resulted in the limit of attaining environmental landscape. The research study aims to analyze the environmental impact due to the migration of Rohingya refugees to ensuing surrounding camp regions on a temporal basis. The study delves into how the spread of camps has altered land use, leading to the gradual eradication of forest and agricultural land and the gradual expansion of urban areas. The Maximum Likelihood Classification in ArcGIS 10.7 and ERDAS Imagine were used to process multispectral Landsat-8 OLI-TIRS images (2013–2021). Land cover shifted significantly over the course of nine years, with built-up areas and Rohingya camps growing by 5.61% and 5.10%, respectively, while forest and agricultural land decreased by 6.20% and 3.81%. The increase in area covered by Rohingya camp almost caught up to urban built-up causing significant impact on landcover areas. Their consistency in evaluating vegetative health and environmental condition was confirmed by multivariate analysis, which revealed a substantial positive correlation between NDVI and EVI (r = 0.94–0.97). LST raised by around 0.12 °C yr − 1 , according to time-series study, whereas NDVI and EVI decreased from 0.67 to 0.51 and 0.68 to 0.48, respectively. This indicates a gradual reduction in plant health within the research region. The research exposes a potential decline in ecosystem health by analyzing changes in vegetation health using remote sensing technologies. The necessity for sustainable solutions is underscored by environmental degradation and resource depletion, which ultimately bolsters the efforts to ensure the secure resettlement of the Rohingya population.

title: Warehouse Automation Strategies and Supply Chain Performance of Oil Servicing Firms in Port Harcourt
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: As technological advancements reshape business operations around the world, warehouse automation strategies have redefined supply chain performance. The study examined the relationship between warehouse automation strategies and the supply
content: As technological advancements reshape business operations around the world, warehouse automation strategies have redefined supply chain performance. The study examined the relationship between warehouse automation strategies and the supply chain performance of oil servicing firms in Port Harcourt. The inability of firms in developing economies to modernize their warehouse activities threatens the sustainability and overall performance. Addressing this gap, the study adopted the resource-based view (RBV) and diffusion of innovation (DOI) theory to extrapolate how warehouse automation strategies relate to the supply chain performance of oil servicing firms in Port Harcourt. And how technology moderates the relationship. Empirical data were gathered through copies of the questionnaire distributed among warehouse managers, production managers, operations managers, and logistics managers of the firms under review. And the results revealed that all dimensions of warehouse automation strategies relate positively with measures of supply chain performance; however, technology does not moderate the relationship between warehouse automation strategies and supply chain performance of oil servicing firms in Port Harcourt. Hence, the study concludes that the adoption of warehouse automation strategies improves the supply chain performance of oil servicing firms in Port Harcourt. Therefore, the study recommends that oil servicing firms in Port Harcourt should invest in modern automation technologies to ensure adequate inventory tracking, automated storage and retrieval systems to improve supply chain visibility, and responsiveness.

title: Process Evaluation of Ironmaking Using In-Flight Hydrogen Plasma Reduction of Partially Pre-reduced Iron Ore
summary: This work evaluates a hybrid ironmaking process that combines hydrogen direct reduction with in-flight hydrogen plasma reduction of iron ore powder using a new reactor, Swin $${\text {H}_2^+}$$ . The reactor uses a non-transferred DC arc pl
content: This work evaluates a hybrid ironmaking process that combines hydrogen direct reduction with in-flight hydrogen plasma reduction of iron ore powder using a new reactor, Swin $${\text {H}_2^+}$$ . The reactor uses a non-transferred DC arc plasma torch with continuous powder injection and was tested with up to 41 kW of electrical power and 9% $$\text {H}_\text {2}$$ -Ar plasma gas. The results suggest that controlling particle residence time is a major challenge for co-current in-flight plasma reactors. As a result, the optimal level of pre-reduction for in-flight systems differs from that for molten-bath reactors. Plasma-reduced iron was found to be less susceptible to reoxidation than direct-reduced iron. However, the current reactor design experienced product losses (>90%), limited metallization (<10%), and high specific energy consumption ( $$\approx$$ 67 kWh/kg of ore, before heat recovery).

title: Livelihood-led Environmental Degradation and its Consequences for Habitability of the Area Around Lake Chivero, Zimbabwe: A Systematic Review
source: Kuveza neKuumba The Zimbabwe Ezekiel Guti University Journal of Design Innovative Thinking and Practice
summary: This systematic review examines how livelihood activities relate to environmental degradation in the Lake Chivero Catchment Area, Zimbabwe, and evaluates the impacts on the area‘s longterm habitability. Motivated by the lake‘s serious ecolo
content: This systematic review examines how livelihood activities relate to environmental degradation in the Lake Chivero Catchment Area, Zimbabwe, and evaluates the impacts on the area‘s longterm habitability. Motivated by the lake‘s serious ecological decline over the past 30 years, despite being a vital water source for over 2.4 million people, a population 10 times its original capacity, the study employs the Social-Ecological Systems (SES) Framework and Institutional Analysis and Development (IAD) Framework. It synthesizes evidence from 67 peer-reviewed studies found through a systematic search of the Scopus, Google Scholar and Web of Science databases, following PRISMA guidelines. Results show that livelihood activities, such as sand mining, brick moulding, urban farming and informal waste disposal, although providing short-term survival benefits, have collectively caused significant environmental harm. Indicators reveal a reduction in lake depth from 28 to 18 metres, an elevenfold increase in nutrient inflows between 2000 and 2012 and sedimentation filling 18% of the lake‘s capacity. Institutional failures, including weak enforcement of environmental laws, underfunded sewage systems and poor governance, have worsened these ecological stresses. The review advocates a comprehensive intervention plan that includes infrastructure upgrades, enforcement of the polluter-pays principle, alternative livelihoods and ecological restoration to prevent a predicted ―2050 Doomsday Scenario‖ in which the lake may become unusable. Without such integrated efforts, the study warns that the lake‘s habitability will remain critically endangered, risking human health and ecological stability.

title: Biological production of synthetic aviation fuels (SAFs) from biomass
summary: Abstract Synthetic aviation fuels (SAFs) produced from biological routes are emerging as a practical way to decarbonize the aviation sector. This review summarizes progress in producing jet-range molecules from renewable carbon and benchmar
content: Abstract Synthetic aviation fuels (SAFs) produced from biological routes are emerging as a practical way to decarbonize the aviation sector. This review summarizes progress in producing jet-range molecules from renewable carbon and benchmarks them against the Jet A and Jet A-1 property window defined by the standard specification for aviation turbine fuels (ASTM D1655). We group candidates into three families, fatty acid-derived streams, alcohol-based precursors, and isoprenoid-derived hydrocarbons, and map their properties and upgrading chemistry to the standard specification for aviation turbine fuel containing synthesized hydrocarbons (ASTM D7566) certification framework. We survey diverse microbial hosts on renewable feedstocks and highlight advances in pathway and chassis engineering and bioprocess intensification that raise titers, productivities, and carbon efficiency. Together, these advances chart a practical route to certified, scalable, and cost-competitive SAF supply.

title: Organic fluorescent metal ion probes for understanding design rules photophysical mechanisms and bioimaging applications
summary: Organic fluorescent probes are widely used for metal-ion detection, yet many reviews remain descriptive and do not explain why different metal ions produce different fluorescence responses. This review addresses that gap by connecting metal
content: Organic fluorescent probes are widely used for metal-ion detection, yet many reviews remain descriptive and do not explain why different metal ions produce different fluorescence responses. This review addresses that gap by connecting metal-ion electronic structure, coordination behavior, and photophysical signal generation for Cu 2+ , Zn 2+ , Fe 3+ , Hg 2+ and Pb 2+ . The central argument is that probe performance depends not only on fluorophore design, but on the compatibility between the target ion and the sensing mechanism. Paramagnetic ions such as Cu 2+ and Fe 3+ usually promote fluorescence quenching through non-radiative decay, intersystem crossing, and charge-transfer pathways, whereas diamagnetic Zn 2+ more readily supports turn-on emission through PET suppression and chelation-induced rigidification. Soft heavy metals such as Hg 2+ and Pb 2+ require carefully selected donor atoms and receptor geometries to balance strong binding, selectivity, and signal reliability. This review compares PET, ICT/TICT, CHEF/CHEQ, ESIPT, energy-transfer, and aggregation-based mechanisms in terms of sensitivity, selectivity, reversibility, water compatibility, and bioimaging utility. The role of DFT and TD-DFT is also discussed as a supporting tool for validating binding modes and excited-state behavior. Overall, this review provides mechanism-guided design principles for developing more selective, photostable, water-compatible, and biologically useful fluorescent metal-ion probes.

title: Optimal control models with random switches and applications to economics and management
summary: Abstract This survey examines the role of stochastic switching times in optimal control theory with a particular emphasis on applications in economics and management. We start with a review of the problem’s formulation and early foundationa
content: Abstract This survey examines the role of stochastic switching times in optimal control theory with a particular emphasis on applications in economics and management. We start with a review of the problem’s formulation and early foundational contributions, followed by an outline of the general model framework. We highlight the structural key components and illustrate the sequence of decision stages. Two main methodological approaches are explored: a backward solution technique and an age-structured (vintage) optimal control formulation. We analyze how both approaches inform the determination and characterization of switching times in the dynamic optimization nexus. The survey further illustrates the relevance of random switching dynamics by applications in environmental economics, health economics and other related domains. Finally, we discuss current challenges and avenues for future research, including the incorporation of multiple switching events, agent heterogeneity, and the consideration of smaller shocks that occur frequently, almost continuously. This synthesis aims to provide both a rigorous theoretical perspective and a practical applied viewpoint on switching times–as critical components of decision-making in economics, finance, management and the broader social sciences–by leveraging mathematical modelling, analytical methods and computational techniques.

title: Mesostigmata mite assemblages in stands developed on former agricultural land
summary: Afforestation of post-agricultural land plays a crucial role in restoring forest soil properties and initiating secondary succession processes driven by soil biota. In this study, we compared Mesostigmata communities in even-aged (21 y./o.)
content: Afforestation of post-agricultural land plays a crucial role in restoring forest soil properties and initiating secondary succession processes driven by soil biota. In this study, we compared Mesostigmata communities in even-aged (21 y./o.) stands of Alnus glutinosa, Betula pendula, Picea abies, Pinus sylvestris, and Tilia cordata established on a former agricultural lands, and adjacent fallow field as a reference habitat, located near the Żelazny Most tailings storage facility (Lubin Forest District, Poland). Soil sampling was conducted on 18 study sites (5 tree species and fallow field × 3 plots) using steel corer (0-15 cm depth), consisting of 90 samples (5 samples from each plot). In total, 592 mesostigmatid mites representing 39 taxa and 15 families were recorded. Community structure differed among habitats, with Alnus glutinosa supporting the highest abundance and diversity, while Tilia cordata exhibited the lowest values. Deciduous stands generally hosted richer and more abundant assemblages than coniferous stands and the fallow field. The occurrence of both widespread generalists and highly specialized species highlights clear habitat differentiation and varying degrees of ecological specialization, reflecting differences in soil restoration processes among tree species.

title: High-Resolution Boundary-Layer Detection Lidar for Spaceborne Applications: Parameter Design, Theoretical Simulation, and Airborne Validation
summary: Abstract. The planetary boundary layer height (PBLH) is a key parameter for studying global land-atmosphere interactions, weather forecasting, and climate change. However, owing to the limited adaptability of existing detection techniques o
content: Abstract. The planetary boundary layer height (PBLH) is a key parameter for studying global land-atmosphere interactions, weather forecasting, and climate change. However, owing to the limited adaptability of existing detection techniques over complex terrain and the lack of observational consistency across different environments, unified and refined boundary layer observations on a global scale remain a major challenge. To support future spaceborne lidar missions for global boundary layer monitoring, this study establishes a closed-loop framework integrating spaceborne parameter design, theoretical simulation, and airborne experimental validation. As a core technical advance, a scaled airborne prototype was developed, and a synergistic terrain-atmosphere detection regime was introduced. By synchronously acquiring surface elevation and atmospheric backscatter signals, the system can directly retrieve the boundary layer height relative to the actual ground surface, namely above ground level (AGL), thereby fundamentally mitigating the terrain-matching bias of conventional approaches. System performance was primarily validated through the Yulin nighttime flight experiment, where the retrieved BLH showed a median difference of 10 m and a maximum RMSE of 45 m relative to the ground-based reference. The additional Hainan daytime flight experiment indicated the system's detection potential under strong background illumination and complex cloud conditions. This study validates the performance of the airborne prototype and provides empirical evidence for the parameter design of future spaceborne detection systems, supporting the construction of a globally consistent and high-precision boundary layer observation network.

title: Multi-Model Analysis for Policy in Agricultural Economics: A Conceptual Framework
summary: The complexity of the issues that practitioners in the field of agricultural economics encounter is increasing, with agriculture intersecting with most of the challenges that society faces.Policies related to agriculture need to address an
content: The complexity of the issues that practitioners in the field of agricultural economics encounter is increasing, with agriculture intersecting with most of the challenges that society faces.Policies related to agriculture need to address an increasing number of objectives, while at the same time it is necessary to understand their related trade-offs.How can policy analysts make use of the available quantitative tools to support an evidence-based policymaking process?In this context, collaborative approaches are increasingly recognised as a vital solution.This paper provides a framework for conducting multi-model analysis for policy and encourages its use in the field of agricultural economics.The following elements are crucial to the success of this method: (i) the development of clear conceptual frameworks identifying the core elements of the problem at hand; (ii) the cooperation between researchers in different fields (or modelling teams); (iii) the identification of synergies and overlaps between models; and (iv) the development of linkages between modelling tools in a largely structured manner.Overall, such an approach ensures that modelling outcomes satisfy policymakers' needs while keeping the modelling tools manageable.The synergistic use of models that are already well-tested in their respective fields enhances the credibility of the results.

title: Multifunctional applications of algae in environmental sustainability, food, agriculture, and biotechnology: current advances and future perspectives
source: World Journal of Biology Pharmacy and Health Sciences
summary: Algae represent a diverse and versatile group of photosynthetic organisms with considerable potential for addressing environmental, agricultural, nutritional, and industrial challenges. This review provides an overview of recent advances in
content: Algae represent a diverse and versatile group of photosynthetic organisms with considerable potential for addressing environmental, agricultural, nutritional, and industrial challenges. This review provides an overview of recent advances in algal biotechnology, with particular emphasis on the multifunctional applications of microalgae, macroalgae, and cyanobacteria in environmental sustainability, food and nutrition, agriculture, and health. In environmental applications, algae can serve as bioindicators of pollution and contribute to the removal of heavy metals, nutrients, and organic contaminants from wastewater and other contaminated environments. Their roles in nitrogen fixation, soil improvement, carbon sequestration, and the development of sustainable agricultural practices are also discussed. From a nutritional perspective, algae provide proteins, essential amino acids, polyunsaturated fatty acids, vitamins, minerals, dietary fiber, polysaccharides, and other bioactive compounds, supporting their incorporation into functional foods, fermented products, meat and dairy formulations, and cereal-based foods. Algal-derived compounds, including carotenoids, phycobiliproteins, polyphenols, polysaccharides, sterols, and bioactive peptides, have demonstrated antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, antidiabetic, and potential anticancer activities, although further clinical evidence is required to establish their therapeutic efficacy. The review also considers the potential of algae as sustainable sources of protein, biofuels, bioplastics, and other value-added bioproducts. Despite these advantages, challenges related to cultivation costs, harvesting, biomass processing, environmental variability, food safety, scalability, regulatory requirements, and economic feasibility continue to limit widespread commercialization. Future advances in strain improvement, integrated cultivation systems, algal–microbial interactions, resource recovery, and algal biorefineries may help overcome these limitations. Overall, algae represent promising biological platforms for developing circular and sustainable solutions across food production, agriculture, environmental management, and biotechnology.

title: Litter quality controls early decomposition rates and thus 14C cycling in old peat
summary: Additional 14 C input in ecosystems is often a concern in radiological assessments, and a secondary pathway exists through litter production and decomposition following atmospheric or belowground uptake of 14 C. To examine how litter qualit
content: Additional 14 C input in ecosystems is often a concern in radiological assessments, and a secondary pathway exists through litter production and decomposition following atmospheric or belowground uptake of 14 C. To examine how litter quality influences this process, a 90-day laboratory incubation was conducted using peat soil amended with labile litter, recalcitrant litter, or an equal mixed-litter treatment. Peat soils contain strongly 14 C-depleted carbon stocks, whereas fresh plant litter introduces modern carbon that enters biologically active pools during decomposition. Litter mass loss was used as an index of early decomposition and microbial processing. Litter treatment significantly affected mass loss (one-way ANOVA, p < 0.001). Labile litter showed the greatest decomposition (35%), whereas recalcitrant litter decomposed least (10%), with the mixed treatment intermediate (22%). Observed mass loss in the mixed treatment did not differ from the value expected from the two single-litter treatments, indicating an additive mixture effect. To interpret these results in a radiocarbon context, a conceptual framework of carbon pools was developed using previously determined percent modern carbon (pMC) values from the same peat system. Bulk peat represented an old carbon endmember, whereas dissolved organic carbon, microbial biomass, and dissolved inorganic carbon formed intermediate pools enriched relative to peat. The results indicate that fresh litter quality can rapidly regulate early decomposition rates and the transfer of modern carbon into active soil pools, even in 14 C-depleted peat. These findings highlight the need to consider fresh organic inputs, alongside peat age, when evaluating carbon cycling and 14 C transfer in peatland systems.

title: Advances in Biodegradation of petroleum hydrocarbons based pollutants by Microbes
source: Journal of Ethnobiology and Environmental Research
summary: Petroleum hydrocarbons are the organic contaminants that accumulate in different ecosystems due to their hydrophobic nature and limited bioavailability, which have raised concerns about their release into the environment. Due to their carci
content: Petroleum hydrocarbons are the organic contaminants that accumulate in different ecosystems due to their hydrophobic nature and limited bioavailability, which have raised concerns about their release into the environment. Due to their carcinogenic and neurotoxic nature a serious threat has been posed to human and environmental health. But the removal of these pollutants from the environment is a challenging task. Conventional treatment techniques like mechanical and chemical approaches are expensive and inefficient for eliminating hydrocarbons from contaminated areas. Bioremediation is a significant approach for the remediation of petroleum hydrocarbon-contaminated environments, using the natural biodegradation activity of microorganisms. Microorganisms that utilize petroleum hydrocarbons are prevalent in the environment. They naturally degrade pollutants and remove them from the environment. Biosurfactants lower surface tension, encourage emulsification, micelle formation, and make hydrocarbons bioavailable for microbial breakdown. So, utilising biosurfactant-producing bacteria can increase the effectiveness of bioremediation (Zhuang et al., 2022). This article provides an overview of bioremediation of petroleum hydrocarbon pollutants. Some crucial, but often overlooked factors which play a key role in the bioremediation are also elucidated. It also provides information about hydrocarbon metabolism in microorganisms with emphasis on new insights gained during the past couple of years. The main aim of this review is to provide a thorough understanding of the distinctive features of hydrocarbon microbiology that could be helpful in organizing further biodegradation studies. It also serves as a springboard for a broader discussion about the shortcomings and potential enhancements of the bioremediation techniques now in use.

title: Engineering Equitable Data Platforms: A Governance Framework for Algorithmic Fairness, Transparency, and Sustainable Decision-Making Infrastructure
source: East African Journal of Information Technology
summary: Data analytics platforms have evolved from internal business tools into critical infrastructure mediating access to economic opportunity across financial services, employment, retail, and civic life. While organisations typically evaluate t
content: Data analytics platforms have evolved from internal business tools into critical infrastructure mediating access to economic opportunity across financial services, employment, retail, and civic life. While organisations typically evaluate these platforms on narrow performance metrics revenue impact, operational efficiency, and decision velocity the platforms simultaneously encode assumptions about populations, replicate historical inequities, and amplify those inequities at the scale and speed of algorithmic decision-making. This article develops a multi-layer governance framework for engineering equitable data platforms, addressing algorithmic fairness, transparency and accountability, environmental sustainability, and the particular governance requirements of vulnerable and underrepresented populations. The article introduces a dual-gatekeeping model that distinguishes between restrictive gatekeeping in which data platforms entrench historical bias through biased training data and historical optimisation criteria and expansive gatekeeping in which platforms are intentionally designed to extend economic opportunity to previously excluded populations. The proposed governance framework integrates six operational dimensions: fairness metric definition and continuous monitoring, representative training data governance, pre-deployment bias testing, continuous post-deployment fairness auditing, data collection governance, and transparency and accountability mechanisms. The article further examines the environmental footprint of data platform infrastructure, arguing that sustainable platform governance must encompass energy accountability and lifecycle stewardship alongside fairness commitments. Finally, the article demonstrates convergence between fairness governance and strategic advantage, repositioning ethical platform design as an organisational imperative rather than a compliance burden. The framework is intended to be operationalizable by data architects, platform engineers, and organisational leaders responsible for consequential algorithmic decision systems.

title: Heavy Metal Determination and Risk Assessment of Selected Mushroom Species and their Substrates in South-eastern Nigeria
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: Heavy metals (HMs) contaminate the environment and pose significant health risks to humans through accumulation in ecosystems, leading to toxicity and various diseases. This study assessed heavy metal contamination and associated risks in s
content: Heavy metals (HMs) contaminate the environment and pose significant health risks to humans through accumulation in ecosystems, leading to toxicity and various diseases. This study assessed heavy metal contamination and associated risks in selected mushroom species and their substrates across southeastern Nigeria. Using a stratified random sampling approach, representative mushroom and substrate samples were collected from five states: Abia, Anambra, Ebonyi, Enugu, and Imo. Soil chemical properties were analyzed using standard methods, while heavy metals were determined using an Atomic Absorption Spectrophotometer (Varian Spectra AA 200). Data were subjected to analysis of variance (ANOVA), and significant means were separated using Duncan’s Multiple Range Test (DMRT) at a 5% probability level. Results showed significant variations in heavy metal concentrations (Pb, Ni, Cr, Fe, and Cd) in both mushrooms and substrates, as well as in soil chemical properties (pH, organic carbon, organic matter, total nitrogen, total phosphorus, electrical conductivity, and cation exchange capacity) across species and sampling locations. The distribution of heavy metals followed the order Fe > Pb > Ni > Cr > Cd in oyster mushrooms and Fe > Pb > Ni > Cd > Cr in Agaricus species. Ebonyi State recorded the highest contamination levels for most heavy metals (Pb, Ni, Cd) in oyster mushrooms, followed by Anambra (Fe) and Abia (Cr). Similarly, Agaricus mushrooms from Ebonyi showed the highest contamination for Pb, Ni, Cr, and Cd, while Anambra recorded higher levels of Fe. For substrates, Agaricus samples from Enugu exhibited the highest pollution levels, whereas oyster mushroom substrates showed higher contamination in Abia (Pb and Cd) and Ebonyi (Ni), followed by Anambra (Fe). Although most risk assessment results indicated non-contaminated to low contamination levels suggesting that the studied locations are relatively safe continuous monitoring of heavy metal concentrations in biological tissues is recommended to prevent long-term bioaccumulation.
