title: Feasibility of Value Propositions Based on Importance Performance Analysis and Risk Using Simulation: Evidence From SMEs
summary: This study examines the feasibility of value propositions in Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) using Importance Performance Analysis (IPA) and risks, applying system dynamics simulation. The IPA plots the indicators in four quadrants to d
content: This study examines the feasibility of value propositions in Small and Medium Enterprises (SMEs) using Importance Performance Analysis (IPA) and risks, applying system dynamics simulation. The IPA plots the indicators in four quadrants to determine which areas should be prioritized for improvement. The issues in this study are the areas with high importance but with low performance such as return guarantees, product design and promotions. System Dynamics simulations are used to evaluate these factors and point to opportunities for action: add personnel to provide return guarantees, increase product design frequency and reallocate promotional budgets. The best improvement efforts are identified by evaluating the feasibility and risks of each alternative to improve the value proposition. This holistic approach provides a strategic framework for SMEs to enhance customer satisfaction, reduce operational costs, and attain sustainable growth.

title: ESG Frameworks and Primary-Care-Amenable Child Mortality: A Global Multi-Method Assessment
summary: Environmental, Social and Governance frameworks are increasingly invoked in health policy, yet their three pillars are almost always studied in isolation and rarely against outcomes that primary care can influence. Using the World Bank Sove
content: Environmental, Social and Governance frameworks are increasingly invoked in health policy, yet their three pillars are almost always studied in isolation and rarely against outcomes that primary care can influence. Using the World Bank Sovereign ESG Data Portal, this study decomposes the determinants of under-five mortality — the canonical primary-care-sensitive outcome and the target of SDG 3.2 — across the full ESG structure. Three equations share the same dependent variable and differ only in their regressor block: Environment (3,533 observations, 174 economies, 2000–2020), Social (2,032 observations, 99 economies, 2001–2023) and Governance (3,592 observations, 176 economies, 2000–2022). Each block is analysed three ways: panel econometrics comprising pooled OLS, one-way and two-way fixed effects, random effects, Between, WLS and dynamic GMM estimators; unsupervised taxonomy comparing six clustering algorithms across eleven internal validation indices; and supervised validation comparing six learners under both random and country-grouped cross-validation. Safely managed drinking water is the only predictor significant in all six static estimators including two-way fixed effects, with a ten-point coverage increase associated with 21% lower mortality within countries, while particulate exposure is robust on both the cross-country and within-country margins. Institutional quality becomes significant across all estimators only after the four Worldwide Governance Indicators, correlated between 0.80 and 0.94, are orthogonalised — a collinearity independently confirmed by unsupervised dimension reduction and by out-of-fold permutation importance. Within-country explanatory power ranks governance ahead of social and environmental blocks, while out-of-sample prediction ceilings run in the opposite order. Machine learning reproduces the econometric hierarchy, reveals a U-shaped renewable-energy relationship and a threshold in institutional capacity, and shows that random train-test splits overstate accuracy by up to 23 points of R2 through country memorisation. ESG determinants of child survival are pillar-specific in both magnitude and functional form: service access dominates, institutional quality matters above a capacity threshold, and environmental exposures act through structural conditions rather than year-on-year change.

title: Kanola Yağından Mikrodalga Destekli Biyodizel Üretiminin Yanıt Yüzey Yöntemi ile Optimizasyonu ve Süreç Analizi
source: Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology
summary: Bu çalışma, kanola yağından sodyum hidroksit (NaOH) katalizörü eşliğinde mikrodalga destekli transesterifikasyon yöntemiyle biyodizel üretimini ve bu sürecin optimizasyonunu ele almaktadır. Geleneksel ısıtma yöntemlerinin aksine mikrodalga
content: Bu çalışma, kanola yağından sodyum hidroksit (NaOH) katalizörü eşliğinde mikrodalga destekli transesterifikasyon yöntemiyle biyodizel üretimini ve bu sürecin optimizasyonunu ele almaktadır. Geleneksel ısıtma yöntemlerinin aksine mikrodalga teknolojisi, reaksiyon sürelerini dakikalar seviyesine indirerek enerji tasarrufu ve yüksek verim sağlamaktadır. Araştırmada; sıcaklık, katalizör miktarı ve süre gibi değişkenlerin etkilerini analiz etmek için Yanıt Yüzey Metodolojisi kullanılmıştır. Elde edilen bulgular, 51,97°C sıcaklık, %0,69 katalizör oranı ve 3,12 dakika gibi ideal koşullarda %93,75 oranında biyodizel verimine ulaşılabildiğini kanıtlamaktadır. Sonuç olarak bu yöntem, çevre dostu ve sürdürülebilir bir enerji alternatifi olan biyodizelin endüstriyel üretim süreçlerini iyileştirmek için etkili bir çözüm sunmaktadır.

title: A Secure Decentralized Blockchain and Machine Learning-Based Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading in a Smart Grid
summary: The growing adoption of renewable energy and small-scale power producers has increased the need for reliable and transparent peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading. Traditional centralized markets often struggle with high transaction fees, limit
content: The growing adoption of renewable energy and small-scale power producers has increased the need for reliable and transparent peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading. Traditional centralized markets often struggle with high transaction fees, limited transparency, and a greater risk of manipulation, which restrict efficient energy distribution. To overcome these issues, this study presents a decentralized P2P trading framework that implements a fully functional blockchain-based trading system with smart grid simulation and demonstrates a prototype machine learning forecasting module (Random Forest, 84% accuracy) designed for future integration. The trading mechanism is developed using Ethereum smart contracts and a custom ERC-20 token, the TUM Energy Coin (TEC), enabling secure and traceable energy exchange. System security is strengthened through dual confirmation steps, role-based access control, and consensus-driven market clearing. A double-sided auction model is used to match buyers and sellers fairly. Real-time grid behavior such as fluctuating loads, prosumer generation, and consumer demand is modeled using MATLAB Simulink to reflect realistic operating conditions. To enhance decision-making, a Random Forest model is integrated for load forecasting and dynamic pricing, achieving an accuracy of 84%. The simulation results show improved transaction throughput, more stable pricing, and strong resilience against false-data injection attacks. The primary novelty of this work lies in (1) an entirely operational and validated blockchain-trading system simulation with synchronized time using Simulink, (2) a working Random Forest forecasting tool demonstrating feasibility for incorporation in the future, and (3) an analysis of the system’s robustness in the case of FDIA attacks. The authors point out that the ML component used is a prototype and not yet integrated into the functioning block chain.

title: Cybernetic Governance for Renewable Energy Systems Using Blockchain: A Framework for Trustworthy Impact Monitoring
summary: The transition toward decentralized renewable energy systems creates monitoring problems that current digital infrastructures do not solve: sustainability claims are produced by the same actors they evaluate, environmental evidence is repor
content: The transition toward decentralized renewable energy systems creates monitoring problems that current digital infrastructures do not solve: sustainability claims are produced by the same actors they evaluate, environmental evidence is reported periodically rather than observed continuously, and the communities most affected by deployment cannot inspect the data used to represent their territories. Existing integrated platforms combine subsets of the blockchain, Internet of Things (IoT) sensing and life cycle assessment (LCA) at the data layer, but they do not organize that integration through an explicit governance structure. This paper contributes a cybernetic governance framework in which the Viable System Model (VSM) supplies the organizing structure of a blockchain–IoT–LCA monitoring architecture, so that sensing, distributed trust, strategic intelligence and participatory governance are recursively coupled rather than sequentially chained. The framework was developed and evaluated under the Design Science Research paradigm, and instantiated in the IMPACT Energy.CO platform across two technology routes, wind and solar, in La Guajira, Cesar, Atlántico and Magdalena, Colombia. Evaluation against six pre-declared criteria reports 45 executed test cases with a 100% pass rate, 90% unit and 87% integration code coverage, load tests up to 5000 concurrent users with zero errors and sub-second mean response, an operating hash-chained provenance layer issuing verifiable LCA certificates, 14 participatory validation workshops, 199 users trained and 166 technicians certified. We use traceability in a deliberately narrow sense throughout: the property whereby a committed record can be linked to the ingested data series, model version and computation that produced it, and its integrity and ordering checked by a party that does not trust the producer. It is provenance and integrity traceability from the point of ingestion onward, and it is not metrological traceability: the architecture cannot verify that an original sensor measurement corresponds to the physical quantity it purports to represent. We accordingly make explicit what the architecture does not guarantee: a ledger protects records after commitment but cannot certify measurement at the point of capture, and we present a threat model, a set of implemented controls and the residual risk that remains. This study contributes an architecture, a reproducible development and evaluation method, and a calibrated account of what verifiable environmental monitoring can and cannot deliver in contested Global-South territories.

title: Water Use of Peppers Treated with Biochar and Irrigated with Wastewater
source: Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology
summary: Drought is one of the most significant risk factors threatening agricultural production today. Managing soil moisture through the application of biochar and using treated wastewater as an alternative irrigation water source to fresh water a
content: Drought is one of the most significant risk factors threatening agricultural production today. Managing soil moisture through the application of biochar and using treated wastewater as an alternative irrigation water source to fresh water are promising approaches to mitigating the effects of drought. This study was conducted in Van province (Türkiye), a semi-arid region, to investigate the effects of varying doses of biochar applications (0, 0.5, 1.5, and 3.0 tons da-1) and different irrigation water qualities (fresh water and treated wastewater) on plant yield, water use potential, and water efficiency of pepper plants (Capsicum annuum L.) using a randomized block design with 3 replications. The results showed that biochar and increasing doses of biochar, and irrigation with treated wastewater compared to fresh water increased pepper yield, decreased irrigation water amount and actual plant water consumption, thus improving water and irrigation water productivity with biochar and treated wastewater. The highest yield increase (16.85%) was obtained at a biochar dose of 3.0 tons da-1. Irrigation with treated wastewater increased yield by 9.75% compared to fresh water and resulted irrigation water saving of approximately 1% on a mean. At a dose of 3.0 tons da-1, biochar application resulted in a mean decrease of 5.21% in irrigation water mount compared to the control. Water and irrigation water productivity increased by 22.42% and 21.26%, respectively, in biochar applications. In irrigation with treated wastewater, water and irrigation water productivity also improved by 10.68% and 10.56%, respectively. In conclusion, applying 3.0 tons da-1 of biochar to the soil and irrigating with treated wastewater in pepper cultivation was found to be recommendable for effective water resource management and sustainable agricultural production under drought conditions. However, further comprehensive studies are needed, and the risks of salinity and heavy metals from treated wastewater should also be considered.

title: A Forecast-Embedded, Uncertainty-Aware Digital Twin for MPC-Coupled Battery Sizing and Multi-Objective Energy Management in PV-Based DC Microgrids
summary: Renewable-rich DC microgrids require energy management that quantifies photovoltaic and load uncertainty rather than merely reacting to it. This paper presents a forecast-embedded Digital Twin (DT) framework in which a hybrid BiLSTM–GPR for
content: Renewable-rich DC microgrids require energy management that quantifies photovoltaic and load uncertainty rather than merely reacting to it. This paper presents a forecast-embedded Digital Twin (DT) framework in which a hybrid BiLSTM–GPR forecaster feeds a Model-Predictive-Control (MPC) battery sizing and dispatch pipeline, propagating the GPR's predictive standard deviation into a time-varying, chance-constrained state-of-charge (SOC) reserve applied identically across four Energy Management Strategies (Rule-Based, MPC, Q-Learning, and Fuzzy Logic), evaluated over a 13-day study with pairwise Wilcoxon signed-rank tests on 200 matched-pair Monte Carlo trials. A train/inference bin-edge inconsistency in the Q-Learning controller is corrected, reducing its Monte Carlo cost variance roughly fivefold. MPC remains the lowest-cost strategy ($8.5259 versus $11.0837, $10.4079, and $11.3823 for Rule-Based, Q-Learning, and Fuzzy Logic), with 100% cost-rank consistency and a 32.65% cost reduction relative to a no-Digital-Twin baseline, though it never achieves the lowest peak grid import across the 13-day set (0.0% peak win-rate), exposing a cost-reliability trade-off. The uncertainty-aware reserve is obtained at essentially no cost, reducing MPC's cost by 4.55% with no measurable change in peak grid import relative to fixed SOC bounds. All pairwise EMS cost distributions differ significantly (p ≤ 3.00×10⁻³¹). Results are reported alongside a 17-item architectural validation checklist.

title: Tourism Development, Environmental Sustainability and Resource Use Dynamics in South Asia
summary: This study investigates the relationship between tourism development and resource-use dynamics in South Asia, focusing on environmental pressure, infrastructure, and structural factors. Using a balanced panel dataset of eight South Asian co
content: This study investigates the relationship between tourism development and resource-use dynamics in South Asia, focusing on environmental pressure, infrastructure, and structural factors. Using a balanced panel dataset of eight South Asian countries over 25 years, the study applies the CS-ARDL model to address cross-sectional dependence, heterogeneity, and mixed integration properties. The findings indicate that carbon emissions are positively and significantly associated with tourism development, suggesting a “dirty growth” pattern in which tourism expansion remains linked to environmentally intensive activities. However, dynamic panel GMM analysis indicates that this positive association is not robust after controlling for endogeneity, warranting caution in its causal interpretation. Conversely, electricity access, water productivity, and trade openness exhibit negative associations with tourism development, reflecting structural inefficiencies and weak support mechanisms. Robustness checks using FMOLS and DOLS provide consistent support for the long-run effects of CO 2 emissions and electricity access, whereas the remaining variables exhibit estimator-sensitive results. Panel Granger causality analysis further identifies a unidirectional predictive relationship from tourism development to carbon emissions, highlighting feedback dynamics between tourism expansion and environmental pressure. Overall, the study highlights the limited decoupling of tourism growth from environmental and resource constraints in South Asia.

title: Following rigorous accuracy and research on constructing scenario sets for combined wind and solar power output based on kernel density estimation and copula functions
summary: The inherent uncertainties of renewable energy sources—specifically their intermittent and volatile nature—create significant obstacles for power system planning. With the growing integration of renewables into the grid, mapping the precise
content: The inherent uncertainties of renewable energy sources—specifically their intermittent and volatile nature—create significant obstacles for power system planning. With the growing integration of renewables into the grid, mapping the precise interdependencies among wind generation, solar photovoltaic (PV) yield, and power demand has become crucial for designing and managing resilient power networks. To address the challenge of simulating representative scenarios for correlated wind and solar outputs, this study initially employs non-parametric kernel density estimation (KDE) to model extensive empirical datasets. Following rigorous accuracy and goodness-of-fit validation, specific KDE formulas for both wind and solar resources are derived. Subsequently, the research constructs various Copula-based joint probability models to represent the combined power generation of wind and solar farms. The performance of these models is comparatively assessed using Maximum Likelihood Estimation (MLE) alongside Akaike and Bayesian Information Criteria (AIC/BIC). reduce nce, the most suitable Copula function is identified to capture the joint probabilistic behavior of wind and PV systems. Ultimately, this optimal Copula model drives the generation of annual power output profiles for wind and solar energy. Computational experiments and validation procedures confirm that the simulated yearly scenarios accurately preserve the underlying correlation structures of the original data.

title: Identifying a gap between decarbonization needs and practical solar and wind deployment in ASEAN
summary: Abstract For decarbonization in ASEAN, large-scale deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind power is widely assumed in scenario-based studies. However, these studies rarely account for the multiple spatial constraints that determine w
content: Abstract For decarbonization in ASEAN, large-scale deployment of solar photovoltaic (PV) and wind power is widely assumed in scenario-based studies. However, these studies rarely account for the multiple spatial constraints that determine where and how renewable energy can practically be deployed. Here, we reveal a gap between decarbonization needs and practical PV and wind deployment in ASEAN using a high-resolution, spatially explicit framework tailored to ASEAN that integrates building footprints, land use and offshore data to quantify practical solar PV and wind deployment across key location types and their underlying constraints. Even if all large rooftops (≥200 m²) were used for PV deployment, they would provide only 683 TWh of electricity, far below the 1,681 TWh required under the IEA Announced Pledges Scenario. Expanding deployment to all relatively low-constraint areas increases generation to only 1,239 TWh, indicating that achieving decarbonization requires development in progressively more constrained locations. We further show that renewable deployment is constrained not only by resource availability but also by the spatial mismatch between renewable resources, electricity demand and transmission infrastructure. We also reveal previously overlooked constraints on rooftop PV deployment, including building characteristics and socioeconomic conditions. These findings demonstrate that renewable deployment pathways are inherently region-specific and require spatially explicit planning tailored to national conditions.

title: Seed Mucilages: From Plant to Biomaterials for Tissue Engineering - A Comparative Review
source: Turkish Journal of Agriculture - Food Science and Technology
summary: Seed mucilages are plant-derived polysaccharides obtained from the seeds of crop and medicinal plant species, including quince (Cydonia oblonga), psyllium (Plantago ovata), flaxseed (Linum usitatissimum), chia (Salvia hispanica), basil (Oci
content: Seed mucilages are plant-derived polysaccharides obtained from the seeds of crop and medicinal plant species, including quince (Cydonia oblonga), psyllium (Plantago ovata), flaxseed (Linum usitatissimum), chia (Salvia hispanica), basil (Ocimum basilicum), and fenugreek (Trigonella foenum-graecum). Their ability to form hydrogels, respond to pH changes, display tunable rheological behavior, and undergo chemical modification has attracted growing interest in biomedical and pharmaceutical research. Despite this growing body of literature, the field remains fragmented: studies are typically limited to a single mucilage source or a narrow application context, and comparative analyses grounded in chemical structure are uncommon. This review addresses that gap by systematically examining six agriculturally accessible seed mucilages within a unified structure–function–application framework. Key compositional parameters, including backbone polysaccharide type, uronic acid content, molecular weight, degree of branching, and surface charge density, are discussed in relation to macroscopic material behaviors such as swelling kinetics, viscoelasticity, film-forming capacity, and biodegradation. These property profiles are contextualized against reported application outcomes in controlled drug delivery, tissue engineering scaffolds, wound dressings, adsorption platforms, and functional films. The review also consolidates findings on persistent limitations, including batch heterogeneity arising from species and extraction variability, methodological inconsistencies in characterization, mechanical weakness of unmodified networks, and incomplete long-term biosafety data, and identifies specific research directions needed for clinical and industrial translation. Taken together, the available evidence suggests that seed mucilages are versatile, sustainably sourced biomaterial components derived from established agricultural and medicinal plant species. By linking crop production, seed processing, mucilage recovery, biopolymer design, and advanced material applications, this review highlights their relevance not only for biomedical systems but also for agricultural waste valorization, value-added product development, food-related materials, and circular bioeconomy strategies.

title: MoRAM for Multi-Step and Multivariate Short-Term Wind-Power Forecasting: A Reproducibility Audit and Corrected Attention Ablation
summary: Accurate short-term wind-power forecasting supports renewable-energy integration. This study presents a reproducibility and implementation audit of MoRAM, an integrated architecture that combines feature-token attention, a residual Mamba la
content: Accurate short-term wind-power forecasting supports renewable-energy integration. This study presents a reproducibility and implementation audit of MoRAM, an integrated architecture that combines feature-token attention, a residual Mamba layer, dense two-expert blending, and a one-dimensional convolution (Conv1D)–linear residual output path to forecast 12 h of normalized turbine power from 48 h multivariate histories in Dataset A (200 turbines; 8760 hourly records). Source reconstruction found that the historical PyTorch attention layer used its default sequence-major interface on batch-major data, thereby mixing samples; the dense-window record is therefore retained only as an implementation audit. We corrected the layer to batch-first feature-token semantics and ran an attention-only ablation using all turbines, a 12 h window-start stride, and five paired seeds. Corrected MoRAM achieved mean absolute error (MAE) 0.2428 ± 0.0029 per unit (p.u.) and root-mean-square error (RMSE) 0.3035 ± 0.0059 p.u.; bypassing only attention achieved MAE 0.2298 ± 0.0027 p.u. and RMSE 0.2839 ± 0.0028 p.u. (mean ± sample standard deviation). The attention-free condition had lower overall MAE and RMSE in every seed and, after averaging across seeds, at every forecast horizon. The principal validated contribution is therefore an auditable reconstruction—complete data protocol, source/log mapping, corrected tensor semantics, and a reproducible five-seed negative ablation—rather than evidence that every constituent module or the integrated architecture is superior.

title: Solar-wind resource characteristics and optimal capacity allocation across China: Insights from observations and reanalyses
summary: Abstract Accurate characterization of renewable energy variability, complementarity, and optimal capacity allocation is essential for power system planning, yet observational evidence and reanalysis performance to reproduce these characteri
content: Abstract Accurate characterization of renewable energy variability, complementarity, and optimal capacity allocation is essential for power system planning, yet observational evidence and reanalysis performance to reproduce these characteristics remain poorly quantified. Using homogenized observations from 1980–2022, this study quantifies solar-wind resource intermittency, availability, and complementarity across China, and assesses the performance of ERA5, MERRA-2, and JRA-55 in reproducing these characteristics. A Compound Synergistic Cost Index is further developed to optimize solar-wind capacity allocation by jointly considering their characteristics and installation cost. Results show that wind energy exhibits higher intermittency (0.45-0.61) than solar energy (0.21-0.40), while hybrid systems significantly reduce intermittency to 0.20-0.37 and enhance resource availability. Strong solar-wind complementarity is concentrated in western China, where solar complementing wind dominates and has strengthened in recent decades, whereas wind complementing solar occurs primarily in Northeast China. Optimal capacity allocation reveals distinct regional patterns, with wind power accounting for 44.1% of installed capacity in Northeast China and solar power accounting for 79.4% and 70.6% in the Tibetan Plateau and Northwest China, respectively. Among reanalyses, ERA5 shows the most reliable overall representation of renewable energy characteristics, optimal solar-wind capacity allocation, and hybrid generation potential across most regions of China. Meanwhile, JRA-55 provides more accurate estimates of optimal capacity allocation in Northeast China and the Tibetan Plateau, whereas MERRA-2 better captures solar-wind complementarity at the daily scale in Northwest China. These findings provide an observational benchmark for evaluating reanalysis performance in representing renewable energy characteristics and optimizing hybrid solar-wind system design under varying climates.

title: Short Run Nexus between Energy Efficiency, Foreign Direct Investment and Policy Dynamics in BRICS Economies: A Panel Data Analysis
source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)
summary: Abstract: This study examines the distributional effects of foreign direct investment, renewable energy consumption, and macroeconomic conditions on energy intensity across BRICS economies over the period 1992 to 2024. Panel quantile regres
content: Abstract: This study examines the distributional effects of foreign direct investment, renewable energy consumption, and macroeconomic conditions on energy intensity across BRICS economies over the period 1992 to 2024. Panel quantile regression is employed at five quantile points from Q10 through Q90, preceded by panel unit root tests to ensure estimation reliability. FDI is not found to exert a significant short run effect on energy intensity across any quantile, suggesting its efficiency benefits operate through long run structural channels. Renewable energy consumption significantly reduces energy intensity from Q25 upward, emerging as the most consistent determinant of energy efficiency improvement across the distribution. Economic growth is found to increase energy intensity across all quantiles, consistent with the early-stage Environmental Kuznets Curve prediction, while trade openness exhibits a sign reversal across the distribution. Fixed effects estimation corroborates the main findings. The study offers the first distributional account of the FDI and energy intensity nexus in BRICS, providing policy relevant insights on investment quality, renewable energy mandates, and trade policy tailored to the heterogeneous energy profiles of individual BRICS economies. Keywords: Energy Intensity, Foreign Direct Investment, Renewable Energy Consumption, BRICS Economies, Panel Quantile Regression, Energy Transition JEL Classification Number: Q43, O13, F21, C21

title: Redesigned Electricity Institutions Integrate All New Central and Decentral Markets Equally Reducing Electricity Costs Substantially and Inducing Dynamic Innovation
summary: The electricity grid is a collective good that tends toward monopoly. It links private electricity generation to private electricity use. Its design converged near-globally at the end of the 20th century. Large-scale producers have separate
content: The electricity grid is a collective good that tends toward monopoly. It links private electricity generation to private electricity use. Its design converged near-globally at the end of the 20th century. Large-scale producers have separated ownership from transmission system operators. Quasi-markets link them. New challenges and opportunities render that design obsolete. Solar and wind energy are low-cost but intermittent. Secondary electricity, decentralized, becomes low-cost as well. Fast switches enable real-time adjustments in electricity production and use. Low-cost High-Voltage Direct Current lines centralize while also enabling decentralized frequency control. Centralizing and decentralizing options do not fit the currently fragmented markets and grid. Their integrated redesign is due. Key design elements include: a multi-layered meshed grid; multiple independent grid nodes; market rules that prohibit ownership of multiple linked nodes; real-time nodal pricing; equal prices for all purchasers at a node; and automatic nodal and full-grid equilibrium. The new driving mechanisms improve electricity system efficiency and resilience, contributing to several SDGs. They include a single real-time integrated market, car batteries replacing in-grid batteries, and system expansion linking to low-cost renewables. Costs are reduced by 1/4 in North America and Northeastern Asia and by 2/3 (!) in Western Europe-Mediterranean, currently highly fragmented.

title: Adverse weather effects on the power production of a utility-scale wind turbine
summary: Wind turbines are commonly characterized under idealized atmospheric conditions, yet real-world operation often occurs in rain and other adverse weather that can substantially alter their aerodynamic performance. Here, we combine nearly 10
content: Wind turbines are commonly characterized under idealized atmospheric conditions, yet real-world operation often occurs in rain and other adverse weather that can substantially alter their aerodynamic performance. Here, we combine nearly 10 years of operational data from a 2.5 MW utility-scale wind turbine with controlled wind-tunnel experiments under heavy rain to quantify these effects and identify the mechanisms underlying rain-induced power losses. All five common adverse weather types examined reduce power production. Rain is the most frequent, occurring during 41.9% of the evaluated turbine operating period, and reduces power output by 6.3% on average, with losses reaching approximately 10% near the rated wind speed. Flow-field and force measurements reveal that droplet impacts generate non-uniform water films and rivulets, triggering premature boundary-layer transition and separation, while droplet splashing-back near the blade frontal region extracts momentum from the near-surface airflow. Together, these mechanisms reduce lift and increase drag; near stall, lift decreases by approximately 10% and drag increases by approximately 17% relative to dry conditions. By bridging long-term field observations with controlled laboratory measurements, this study establishes a mechanistic basis for predicting rain-induced turbine performance losses and highlights the need to account for precipitation in turbine design, control, and power-production forecasting.

title: Towards π-ports: System characterization, integrated framework and future research
summary: Achieving a sustainable and resilient logistics system under the Physical Internet (PI or π) paradigm hinges critically on the readiness of maritime ports to enable the required transformation. As a potentially high-friction point in the mo
content: Achieving a sustainable and resilient logistics system under the Physical Internet (PI or π) paradigm hinges critically on the readiness of maritime ports to enable the required transformation. As a potentially high-friction point in the movement of physical goods, a harmonized framework that enables seamless π-port operations is needed. This paper develops such a framework to guide the systematic transformation of π-ports through a systematic literature review and a bibliometric analysis of research on port transformation, smart ports, and PI logistics. The proposed four-layer π-port framework integrates the Physical Layer, Digital Layer, Business and Financial Transactions Layer, and Governance and Decision Layer into a coherent architecture, and connects infrastructure, information flows, business transactions, value mechanisms, and multi-level decision-making. Rather than treating these dimensions in isolation, as existing port studies tend to do, the framework explicates their interdependencies as a prerequisite for effective π-port functioning. Priority research challenges are identified across interoperability standards, synchromodal coordination, decentralized governance, adaptive real-time decision-making, and national and local port contexts. By integrating physical operations, digital systems, business models, and governance into a single conceptual framework, this study provides an interdisciplinary foundation for researchers, port planners, and policymakers pursuing the transition to hyperconnected, resilient, and sustainable maritime logistics systems.

title: Wind and solar forecast data
summary: This dataset contains one year of photovoltaic power generation data and wind speed data used in the study “Optimal scheduling of electric arc furnaces with multiple flexible resources”. The data were used Optimal schedulingto characterize
content: This dataset contains one year of photovoltaic power generation data and wind speed data used in the study “Optimal scheduling of electric arc furnaces with multiple flexible resources”. The data were used Optimal schedulingto characterize renewable energy availability and to provide input data for the optimal scheduling model. The dataset supports the analysis of the coordinated operation of electric arc furnace loads and multiple flexible energy resources.

title: Evaluation of a rooftop photovoltaics parameterization in the PALM model system using eddy-covariance observations
summary: The rapid expansion of rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems in urban areas provides substantial renewable energy capacity while also altering the local urban microclimate through changes in roof radiative properties, surface temperature, and r
content: The rapid expansion of rooftop photovoltaic (PV) systems in urban areas provides substantial renewable energy capacity while also altering the local urban microclimate through changes in roof radiative properties, surface temperature, and roof-atmosphere heat exchange. Despite growing observational and mesoscale modelling studies, building-resolving large-eddy simulation investigations with direct comparison to rooftop measurements remain rare. In this study, we evaluate the rooftop PV parameterization in PALM for urban microclimate applications using observations from a rooftop PV system near Dresden, Germany. The evaluation uses three clear-sky, weak-wind cases from late summer to winter, with measurements of radiation, PV surface temperature, eddy-covariance sensible heat flux, Doppler lidar wind profiles, and PV power output. The simulations reproduce incoming radiation well and capture the main diurnal timing of PV surface temperature, sensible heat flux, and power output. Simulated PV surface temperature captures the observed diurnal cycle, but with a reduced amplitude (R 2 = 0.98, slope = 0.79). The model underestimates daytime surface temperature and overestimates nighttime surface temperature, with MB and RMSE values of 1.4 and 4.1 °C. Sensible heat flux shows substantial agreement (R 2 = 0.86), but the amplitude is reduced (slope = 0.79) and the mean bias is negative (MB = −22.0 W m −2 ), with an RMSE of 36.5 W m −2 . PV power output follows the observed diurnal shape and peak timing (R 2 = 0.98), but the amplitude is overestimated (slope = 1.15) and the mean bias is positive (MB = 14.0 kW), with an RMSE of 23.7 kW. Compared with the No-PV case, the PV case shows stronger daytime surface heating and roof-atmosphere heat exchange. Sensitivity experiments show limited effects of grid refinement from 5 m to 2 m but stronger sensitivity to PV layout representation. A uniform fractional PV layout provides a useful approximation for roof-mean surface temperature, whereas a layout preserving the PV arrangement is preferable for sensible heat flux and power output. These results provide a basis for further testing the PALM rooftop PV parameterization in more complex urban and meteorological settings.

title: THERMAL ENVIRONMENT IMPROVEMENT AND PARAMETER OPTIMIZATION OF WET CURTAIN FAN VENTILATION IN A GREENHOUSE: A CFD STUDY WITH EXPERIMENTAL VALIDATION
summary: Effective cooling is crucial for maintaining suitable thermal environments in greenhouses during hot summers. This study developed a coupled numerical model to investigate the cooling performance of a wet curtain system in a multi-span plas
content: Effective cooling is crucial for maintaining suitable thermal environments in greenhouses during hot summers. This study developed a coupled numerical model to investigate the cooling performance of a wet curtain system in a multi-span plastic greenhouse in Weifang, China. Relative deviations were less than 5.88% for wet curtain outlet temperature and below 7% for average greenhouse temperature. Results indicated that the wet curtain reduced the average greenhouse temperature by 2.33 ~ 4.20 ℃, with the maximum reduction of 4.20 ℃ occurring at 12:00. The cooling capacity increased with rising solar radiation in the morning and then diminished in the afternoon. The cooled air entered as a floor-level jet, accumulated near the crop zone, and subsequently rose due to buoyancy, forming two large recirculation vortices that enhanced vertical mixing and improved temperature uniformity. Consequently, the average indoor air velocity increased by 8.38% ~ 22.40% compared to ventilation without the wet curtain. Parametric analysis revealed that the average greenhouse temperature decreased nonlinearly with increasing inlet velocity, and the marginal cooling benefit dropped significantly when the inlet velocity exceeded 0.75 m/s. An optimal inlet velocity range of 0.75 ~ 1.0 m/s is recommended. The model accurately captured the thermal performance and airflow patterns of the greenhouse with wet curtain cooling.

title: Toward Diesel-Range Fuel Properties: Catalytic Cracking of Waste Cooking Oil Biodiesel over Acid-Activated Bentonite
summary: Rising global energy demand and the environmental burden of waste cooking oil (WCO) disposal underscore the urgency of developing cost-effective and sustainable production pathways for renewable fuels similar to diesel fuel. However, WCO-bi
content: Rising global energy demand and the environmental burden of waste cooking oil (WCO) disposal underscore the urgency of developing cost-effective and sustainable production pathways for renewable fuels similar to diesel fuel. However, WCO-biodiesel often exhibits physicochemical properties that differ from those of diesel fuel, prompting quality-enhancement strategies that avoid the costs and complexity of hydrogen-assisted processes. In this study, catalytic upgrading of WCO-biodiesel was conducted in a rotary oven reactor for 1 hour using unactivated bentonite and HCl-activated bentonite at catalyst loadings of 0.20–0.80 wt%, followed by characterization of density, kinematic viscosity, calorific value, flash point, FTIR functional groups, and GC–MS composition distribution. The upgrading products exhibited stable density in the range of 0.842–0.844 g/cm³ across all treatments, while viscosity decreased significantly from 4.94 cSt (WCO) to 3.54–3.55 cSt at 0.20–0.40 wt% before increasing at higher concentrations (4.82 cSt at 0.60 wt% and 4.50 cSt at 0.80 wt%). The calorific value ranged from 10,100 to 11,258 cal/g, with the best performance observed in treatment B (11,258 cal/g), accompanied by a stable flash point of 58.5 °C, whereas lower concentrations produced more volatile fuels (50–52 °C). The FTIR spectrum retained the characteristic dominant ester/aliphatic profile, and the GC–MS area ratio indicated a redistribution between the light fraction (RT < 16 min) and the FAME-rich fraction, demonstrating selective compositional adjustment rather than fundamental structural changes. This study demonstrates a hydrogen-free, clay-based improvement pathway and identifies catalyst-amount-dependent considerations that enable the adjustment of WCO-biodiesel toward handling and energy characteristics similar to those of diesel fuel.

title: Robust optimization of hydrogen-containing integrated energy systems
summary: This study investigates the optimal dispatch of integrated energy systems incorporating conventional electrolyzers. Building on traditional electrolyzer technology, we further integrate electrolyzers with renewable energy-based integrated e
content: This study investigates the optimal dispatch of integrated energy systems incorporating conventional electrolyzers. Building on traditional electrolyzer technology, we further integrate electrolyzers with renewable energy-based integrated energy systems. Through multi-stage robust scheduling models and real-time economic dispatch models, we address the unpredictability and robustness challenges in dispatching integrated energy systems under various uncertainties for both single-unit and multi-unit hydrogen production facilities. This approach unlocks the potential of hydrogen-integrated energy systems and enhances operational performance.

title: FFCS-Net: controlled multi-prior interaction via decoupled residual gating for lightweight defect detection
source: Journal of King Saud University - Computer and Information Sciences
summary: Embedding domain priors can compensate for the limited capacity of lightweight defect detectors, yet existing methods implicitly treat prior stacking as beneficial, overlooking the nonlinear interactions—synergy, perturbation, or conflict—t
content: Embedding domain priors can compensate for the limited capacity of lightweight defect detectors, yet existing methods implicitly treat prior stacking as beneficial, overlooking the nonlinear interactions—synergy, perturbation, or conflict—that may arise when heterogeneous inductive biases are injected simultaneously into the same information flow. This paper addresses this gap within the scope of lightweight steel surface defect detection. We propose FFCS-Net, a controlled feature selection framework that decouples three inductive biases—edge gradient, scale preference, and detail preservation—using learnable residual scaling factors for independent intensity adjustment of edge and detail priors, while scale preference is regulated through SE channel gating; the framework is lightweight in parameter count, approximately 2.0M, at a moderate inference-speed trade-off that remains acceptable for offline industrial inspection. Through an eight-run full factorial ablation, we uncover a synergy-disturbance-boundary progression pattern of multi-prior interactions: edge and scale priors exhibit near-linear synergy with a gain ratio of approximately 0.97 on NEU-DET; adding the detail prior induces P-R imbalance on Aero-Engine with a gap of 33.19%, narrowed to 2.79% via scaling factor control; under extreme class imbalance, SE channel gating suppresses minority classes, a failure circumvented by feature concatenation. Experiments on NEU-DET, Aero-Engine, and GC10-DET validate these findings, suggesting that the injection intensity, rather than the mere presence, of inductive biases governs their interaction outcomes in lightweight detector design.

title: ENHANCING RAW MATERIAL RECOVERY THROUGH COLUMN FLOTATION TECHNOLOGY IN SAUDI ARABIA'S MINING INDUSTRY
source: Veredas do Direito Direito Ambiental e Desenvolvimento Sustentável
summary: Mining is being reoriented in Saudi Arabia as a strategic industrial pillar, with the recovery of raw materials becoming a core focus of competitiveness, environmental stewardship and national supply-chain resilience. This review paper eval
content: Mining is being reoriented in Saudi Arabia as a strategic industrial pillar, with the recovery of raw materials becoming a core focus of competitiveness, environmental stewardship and national supply-chain resilience. This review paper evaluates column flotation technology as a facilitator for improving the recovery of phosphate, copper, zinc, gold-bearing sulphides, industrial minerals and future critical-mineral streams in the Kingdom. The paper is a structured review, inspired by the recent Springer open-access formatting, from context and objectives to a transparent methodology, thematic synthesis, technology assessment, implementation framework and research agenda. Column flotation is considered because it provides a tall separation zone, controlled air dispersion, froth washing, less mechanical turbulence, and higher selectivity for fine particles compared to many conventional cells. The review integrates evidence from mineral processing, fine particle flotation, nanobubble-assisted flotation, process water recycling, tailings valorisation and mining priorities of Saudi Vision 2030. It argues the biggest opportunity is not just higher concentrate grade but also the creation of a recovery architecture where lost values in slimes, historic tailings and complex feeds are systematically reprocessed. The technology is most promising for Saudi mining operations when coupled with mineralogical characterisation, pilot testing, digital froth monitoring, reagent optimisation, water-quality control, and circular-economy metrics. The review concludes that column flotation can improve raw material recovery, reduce entrainment, water losses and downstream smelting penalties, but successful deployment requires site-specific design, workforce capability, pilot scale validation and integration with national industrial clusters.

title: Valorisation énergétique des boues de vidange en Côte d'Ivoire : potentiel, contraintes et perspectives
summary: La gestion des boues de vidange constitue un défi majeur en Côte d’Ivoire, où l’assainissement autonome domine largement. Cependant, ces boues représentent une ressource énergétique potentielle à travers la production de biogaz ou de combus
content: La gestion des boues de vidange constitue un défi majeur en Côte d’Ivoire, où l’assainissement autonome domine largement. Cependant, ces boues représentent une ressource énergétique potentielle à travers la production de biogaz ou de combustibles solides. Cet article analyse le potentiel de valorisation énergétique des boues en s’appuyant sur des données issues des stations de traitement de boues de vidange (STBV). Les résultats montrent une production croissante de boues, avec une capacité actuelle de traitement de 678 m³/jour et un potentiel projeté de plus de 1700 m³/jour. Malgré ce potentiel, la valorisation énergétique reste marginale. Les contraintes identifiées sont techniques, institutionnelles et économiques. L’étude met en évidence la nécessité d’intégrer ces ressources dans une logique d’économie circulaire.

title: Boiler Efficiency Improvement Through Analysis of Losses
source: International Journal of Science and Research (IJSR)
summary: The increasing demand for electricity, caused by global industrialization and urbanization, necessitates highly efficient energy generation technologies. Coal remains a popular choice due to its abundance and cost-effectiveness. Utility boi
content: The increasing demand for electricity, caused by global industrialization and urbanization, necessitates highly efficient energy generation technologies. Coal remains a popular choice due to its abundance and cost-effectiveness. Utility boilers play a pivotal role in this situation, acting as closed systems that process coal and generate steam by transferring heat energy to water. To address the difficulties inherent in boiler systems, a multidisciplinary effort was made to identify and thoroughly study their operating aspects. This project aims to discover and quantify the effects of each component influencing boiler performance, with a particular emphasis on predicting their values for user-specified loads. The successful execution of derived techniques is critical in reducing heat losses across various thermal components in the boiler system. By improving solutions, aberrant behavior can be avoided. Two approaches, namely data mining-based clustering and neural network-based clustering, were utilized to extract essential insights from thermal data. Furthermore, multiple regression analysis was applied to predict heat absorption patterns. Insights gleaned from clustered patterns enable the definition of optimal set points, which play a crucial role in enhancing operational efficiency and promoting sustainability in power generation.

title: Predictive modeling and discovery of double perovskite oxides for photovoltaics
summary: Discovery of potential oxide perovskites for solar photovoltaic applications remains a key challenge because of the size of the compositional space and the computational cost of first-principal methods. A multi-phase machine learning framew
content: Discovery of potential oxide perovskites for solar photovoltaic applications remains a key challenge because of the size of the compositional space and the computational cost of first-principal methods. A multi-phase machine learning framework has been developed in this study for the prediction of electronic band gaps following a systematic feature selection and hierarchical integration of classification and regression models. By employing XGBoost classification model and weighted voting ensemble regression model which demonstrated superior predictive performance, 592 charge neutral and geometrically formable oxide perovskite compositions were identified within the photovoltaic relevant band gap range of 1.28–1.62 eV. This set was subsequently refined to 38 compositions upon the application of elemental sustainability and manufacturability constraints. These 38 structures are presented as band-gap compatible candidates prioritized for future validation.

title: Integration of Smart Grid Technology for Sustainable Power Distribution: A Case Study of Nigeria
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF COMPUTER SCIENCE AND MATHEMATICAL THEORY E-ISSN
summary: This study explores the integration of smart grid technology as a solution to the persistent energy crises in Nigeria. The aim is to evaluate the feasibility of transitioning from traditional aging infrastructure to a modernized smart grid
content: This study explores the integration of smart grid technology as a solution to the persistent energy crises in Nigeria. The aim is to evaluate the feasibility of transitioning from traditional aging infrastructure to a modernized smart grid to enhance operational reliability and efficiency. The scope covers the current challenges of the Nigerian power sector, including high technical losses and inadequate generation. The methodology employed a qualitative research design involving a systematic literature review, stakeholder interviews with regulatory officials, and analysis of pilot smart grid projects. Data collection was derived from industry reports, academic publications, and real-world performance metrics from distribution companies (DisCos). Findings indicate that implementing Advanced Metering Infrastructure (AMI) can reduce technical losses by up to 15% and increase revenue collection by 25%. However, high upfront costs and a lack of local technical expertise remain significant barriers. The study concludes that a phased implementation approach is vital for long-term success. It is recommended that the Nigerian government establish a robust regulatory framework and prioritize public-private partnerships to bridge the funding and infrastructure gaps.

title: Nanobiotechnological enhancement of bioethanol production from potato peel waste using green-synthesized ZnO nanoparticles
summary: The growing demand for sustainable energy and effective waste management has intensified interest in bioethanol production from agro-industrial residues. This study investigates the potential of potato peel waste (PPs) as an economical subs
content: The growing demand for sustainable energy and effective waste management has intensified interest in bioethanol production from agro-industrial residues. This study investigates the potential of potato peel waste (PPs) as an economical substrate for enhanced bioethanol production using a nanobiotechnological approach. Zinc oxide nanoparticles (ZnONPs) were green-synthesized using potato peel extract and characterized through SEM, EDX, and zeta analysis, confirming their nanoscale size, stability, and elemental composition. An alkali-thermophilic bacterial strain, Bacillus licheniformis (OQ740163), exhibiting both amylolytic and cellulolytic activities, was employed for biomass hydrolysis. The incorporation of ZnONPs significantly enhanced saccharification efficiency, yielding a maximum reducing sugar concentration of 9.58 g/L compared to 5.91 g/L without nanoparticles, representing a 61.96% increase. Subsequent fermentation using Saccharomyces cerevisiae K7 further demonstrated improved ethanol production, achieving a yield of 0.460 g/g glucose compared to 0.399 g/g in the control. The findings highlight the catalytic role of ZnONPs in enhancing both hydrolysis and fermentation processes. Overall, this study presents a sustainable and cost-effective strategy for converting potato peel waste into bioethanol, contributing to renewable energy production and circular bioeconomy development.

title: Knowledge Accuracy and Response Characteristics of an On-Device Large Language Model in Building Environmental Engineering: a Preliminary Case Study of EXAONE 4.0 1.2B Using ChatGPT-4o as a Cloud Reference
summary: This preliminary case study examines EXAONE 4.0 1.2B, an on-device large language model (LLM), in building environmental engineering, using ChatGPT-4o as a high-capability cloud reference rather than a size-matched competitor. Ten Korean-la
content: This preliminary case study examines EXAONE 4.0 1.2B, an on-device large language model (LLM), in building environmental engineering, using ChatGPT-4o as a high-capability cloud reference rather than a size-matched competitor. Ten Korean-language items were evaluated: four multiple-choice, three single-step calculations, and three short-answer questions covering indoor environmental quality, energy, and post-occupancy evaluation. The same simple prompt condition was applied to both models, with no model-specific prompt optimization; therefore, the results represent one standardized condition rather than each model’s maximum performance. Both models answered all seven objective items correctly, although EXAONE showed terminology confusion in its reasoning on a thermal-environment item. Five doctoral-level experts rated the short-answer responses for accuracy, completeness, and logical consistency. Mean scores were 4.18 for ChatGPT-4o and 2.98 for EXAONE. Fleiss’ kappa was 0.020 and 0.044, while free-marginal kappa was 0.333 and 0.222, respectively; the latter values indicate fair, not moderate, agreement, so absolute expert scores require cautious interpretation. Qualitatively, ChatGPT-4o more consistently organized responses around concepts and scope, whereas EXAONE tended to provide specific technical, operational, and Korean-regulatory content but occasionally omitted canonical elements or added unsupported detail. Because the item pool is small and only one on-device model was tested, the findings are exploratory and cannot be generalized to building environmental engineering as a whole or to on-device LLMs as a class. The results support further investigation of on-device LLMs as supervised offline assistants where connectivity or external data transmission is constrained, but not as unsupervised tools for engineering calculation or compliance decisions.

title: Resilience Waterfront Housing Models For Sustainable Community Development in The Niger Delta
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF GEOGRAPHY AND ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT
summary: The Niger Delta region of Nigeria confronts a critical housing deficit compounded by annual flooding, sea level rise, and rapid urbanisation. This paper examined resilient waterfront housing models as strategic interventions for sustainable
content: The Niger Delta region of Nigeria confronts a critical housing deficit compounded by annual flooding, sea level rise, and rapid urbanisation. This paper examined resilient waterfront housing models as strategic interventions for sustainable community development in this ecologically vulnerable region. Through a qualitative multi-case study design incorporating document analysis, secondary data synthesis, and observational assessment of existing housing typologies, this research evaluates the structural integrity, environmental compatibility, and socio-economic viability of three resilient housing approaches: amphibious architecture, elevated pile dwellings adapted with modern materials, and integrated solar-powered estate models. The study draws empirical insights from recent NDDC emergency shelter projects, the Brooks Haven solar estate in Port Harcourt, and comparative vernacular adaptations from the Tempe Lake floating settlements. Findings reveal that the hybridisation of indigenous building knowledge with modern engineering offers the most viable path toward flood resilience and energy autonomy. The analysis further demonstrates that inter-agency collaboration between the Federal Ministry of Housing and the Niger Delta Development Commission creates institutional frameworks capable of scaling these models from pilot projects to community wide implementation. The paper contributes a resilience assessment framework for evaluating waterfront housing interventions and provides policy recommendations for integrating resilient design into Nigeria's national housing agenda.

title: STUDY AND OPTIMIZATION OF THE EFFICIENCY OF A VERTICAL-JUNCTION SILICON SOLAR CELL IN SERIES UNDER A MAGNETIC FIELD IN STEADY STATE
source: World Journal of Advanced Research and Reviews
summary: This article presents a theoretical study of a vertical-junction silicon solar cell in steady state under polychromatic illumination and subjected to an external magnetic field. After solving the magnetotransport equation for minority charg
content: This article presents a theoretical study of a vertical-junction silicon solar cell in steady state under polychromatic illumination and subjected to an external magnetic field. After solving the magnetotransport equation for minority charge carriers in the base using the boundary conditions applied at the junctions and in the rear region, the expressions for the photovoltage, electrical power, and conversion efficiency of the photovoltaic cell are determined as functions of the magnetic field and the optimal thickness of the base. The current-voltage and power-voltage characteristics are studied for several values of the applied magnetic field. Finally, the photovoltaic cell’s efficiency is studied as a function of the optimal base thickness obtained based on the applied magnetic field. This study shows a linear correlation between these two parameters.

title: Fuzzy Analytical Hierarchy Process Model for Malaria Control Strategies Prioritization in North-East, Nigeria
source: Mikailalsys Journal of Mathematics and Statistics
summary: Although the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (F-AHP) is widely used to address complex multi-criteria decision-making problems under uncertainty, its application to malaria intervention prioritization in resource-constrained settings, part
content: Although the Fuzzy Analytic Hierarchy Process (F-AHP) is widely used to address complex multi-criteria decision-making problems under uncertainty, its application to malaria intervention prioritization in resource-constrained settings, particularly North-East Nigeria, remains limited. This study developed and applied an F-AHP decision-support framework to prioritize malaria control interventions based on epidemiological, economic, operational, and social considerations. A mixed-methods approach involved 18 purposively selected experts, including epidemiologists, medical doctors, and health educators from the six states of North-East Nigeria. Primary data were collected through structured questionnaires, while secondary evidence was drawn from peer-reviewed literature, national malaria control guidelines, and relevant health reports. Five evaluation criteria and five intervention alternatives were assessed using fuzzy pairwise comparison matrices. Expert judgments were represented by triangular fuzzy numbers and defuzzified using the centroid method to generate normalized priority weights and global intervention rankings. All judgment matrices met the recommended consistency threshold (CR ≤ 0.10), supporting the internal consistency of the evaluations. Acceptability emerged as the most influential criterion (0.387), followed by cost-effectiveness (0.283) and health impact (0.200). Among the intervention alternatives, insecticide-treated nets/long-lasting insecticidal nets ranked first, with a global priority weight of 0.346, followed by indoor residual spraying at 0.278. These findings demonstrate that social acceptability, economic efficiency, and health impact are central determinants of malaria intervention priorities in the region. The study contributes to fuzzy multi-criteria decision-making in public health by providing a transparent and systematic framework for incorporating uncertainty into expert judgments. Practically, the framework can support policymakers, malaria control programmes, and public health stakeholders in allocating limited resources and selecting contextually appropriate interventions in North-East Nigeria. It also provides a foundation for integrating stochastic and adaptive approaches into future malaria intervention prioritization under temporal and epidemiological uncertainty.

title: Power Sector Reform and Industrial Development in Nigeria: A Study of Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) Port Harcourt Region
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: This study investigated the impact of power sector reforms on industrial development in Nigeria, with specific focus on the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) power transmission operations in Rivers State. The study aimed to identify app
content: This study investigated the impact of power sector reforms on industrial development in Nigeria, with specific focus on the Transmission Company of Nigeria (TCN) power transmission operations in Rivers State. The study aimed to identify approaches adopted by TCN in enhancing power transmission to industries and analyze the impacts of TCN power transmission on industrial development. The research adopted a descriptive survey design, utilizing both primary and secondary data sources. From a population of 592 TCN employees, 239 questionnaires were administered using stratified random sampling technique, with 212 usable questionnaires retrieved representing 88.7% response rate from the Port Harcourt Regional Transmission Company. Data analysis utilized descriptive and inferential statistics through SPSS version 25.0. Key findings revealed that direct wheeling of power emerged as the most effective approach adopted by TCN (mean = 3.38), with transmission operations demonstrating significant positive impacts on industrial development, particularly in boosting Rivers State's IGR through industrial profits (mean = 3.05). An extremely strong correlation (r = 0.986) was established between TCN's impacts and industrial development. The study recommends strengthening direct wheeling capability of TCN and implementing climate-resilient infrastructure measures to optimize TCN's contribution to Rivers State's industrial development.

title: High-Efficiency Novel Cu₃InSnS₅ Quantum Dot Photovoltaics: From Quantum Confinement Modeling to Tandem Cell Optimization for Dual Indoor/Outdoor Energy Harvesting
source: ECS Journal of Solid State Science and Technology
summary: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive numerical optimization of single and tandem photovoltaic cells utilizing novel Cu₃InSnS₅ colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) as absorbers. These quaternary CQDs have emerged as a compelling class of lo
content: Abstract This study presents a comprehensive numerical optimization of single and tandem photovoltaic cells utilizing novel Cu₃InSnS₅ colloidal quantum dots (CQDs) as absorbers. These quaternary CQDs have emerged as a compelling class of low-dimensional materials due to their tunable optoelectronic properties and compliance with the Restriction of Hazardous Substances (RoHS) directive. A multi-scale simulation framework is employed, combining the envelope function approximation to predict size-dependent quantum confinement effects, Rigorous Coupled-Wave Analysis (RCWA) for optical modeling, and the Solar Cell Capacitance Simulator (SCAPS-1D) for device-level electrical optimization. By systematically tuning the CQD radius, buffer layer, and absorber thickness, the optimized single-junction cell achieves a power conversion efficiency of 11.53% under standard AM1.5G illumination, significantly surpassing the current experimental benchmark of <0.1%. Furthermore, a tandem architecture is designed to minimize thermalization losses, yielding an impressive efficiency of 31.97% under AM1.5G. Under indoor LED illumination (1250 lx), the single and tandem cells attain efficiencies of 12.13% and 22.21%, respectively. These findings underscore the immense potential of Cu₃InSnS₅ CQDs for dual indoor/outdoor energy harvesting, particularly for powering low-light Internet of Things (IoT) devices.

title: An Overview of Liberal Ideology and Democracy in Nigeria’s Fourth Republic, 1999-2023
source: INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF SOCIAL SCIENCES AND MANAGEMENT RESEARCH
summary: The crux of this paper is an overview of liberal ideology and democracy within the context of the Nigerian Fourth Republic, spanning from 1999 to 2023. The Nigerian Fourth Republic, established in 1999, is characterized by a complex relatio
content: The crux of this paper is an overview of liberal ideology and democracy within the context of the Nigerian Fourth Republic, spanning from 1999 to 2023. The Nigerian Fourth Republic, established in 1999, is characterized by a complex relationship between liberal ideology and democratic practice. The amended 1999 Constitution lays out a federal framework that includes the separation of powers, fundamental human rights, and guarantees for free and fair elections. Nigeria functions under a multi-party system, with regular elections designed to promote popular participation and representation. The constitution underscores the importance of the rule of law, striving to ensure equality before the law and accountability for all citizens and institutions. The primary aim of this study is to explore liberal ideology and democracy in the Nigerian Fourth Republic from 1999 to 2023. The research employs liberal theory as its theoretical framework and utilizes qualitative research analysis methods. The methodology incorporates secondary data sources, such as online materials, articles, journals, and textbooks. The data collected were qualitatively analyzed through content analysis techniques. The findings indicate that although the constitution and political framework are intended to embody liberal democratic principles, the actual situation often falls short. Challenges such as weak institutions, corruption, military influence, ethnic and regional divisions, limited public engagement, and a lack of robust ideological foundations within political parties impede the full realization of liberal democratic ideals. Based on these findings, the study concludes that Nigeria requires purposeful leadership with a vision that prioritizes its citizens in the administrative agenda, moving beyond limited public participation. The study advocates for strengthening institutions, tackling corruption, and fostering a more inclusive and participatory democracy.
