All pathways achieved substantial GHG savings relative to fossil fuels, with carbon intensities ranging from 3.9 to 25.8 g CO 2 e MJ −1 and GHG emissions savings of 73–96 %, thus remaining well above the 65 % RED minimum GHG emissions reduction threshold. UCO hydroprocessing delivered the lowest carbon intensities, while FCC pathways showed higher values, due to lower liquid-fuel yields and greater upstream burdens. Extrapolating the representative case-study yields to the entire EU refining system, a theoretical biofuel potential of up to 13.9 Mt y −1 at 5 % bio-share at conversion unit inlet is estimated.

title: Assessing distributional and environmental impacts of ETS2 and potential mitigation under the Social Climate Fund
summary: Extended abstract 3-290-26 This submission provides an ex-ante assessment of the distributional impacts of the EU Emissions Trading System for buildings and road transport (ETS2) on households across the 27 EU Member States and assess the r
content: Extended abstract 3-290-26 This submission provides an ex-ante assessment of the distributional impacts of the EU Emissions Trading System for buildings and road transport (ETS2) on households across the 27 EU Member States and assess the role of the Social Climate Fund (SCF) in mitigating these impacts. Carbon pricing in these sectors is central to achieving EU climate neutrality but raises concerns about regressive effects and affordability for vulnerable groups. This presentation addresses methodological challenges in identifying low-income households affected by energy and transport poverty. The work outlined in contains two main parts: First, using the Green EUROMOD microsimulation model based on EU Household Budget Survey (HBS) and EU Statistics on Income and Living Conditions (EU-SILC) data, it estimates household level impacts of ETS2 related price increases. Based on these results, the presentation identifies population groups most exposed to ETS2. It documents substantial heterogeneity across income groups, household characteristics, and countries, driven by differences in consumption patterns, heating technologies, and transport dependence. In the second part, the presentation simulates hypothetical mitigating measures eligible under the SCF, covering both buildings and transport. Measures include direct income support, renovation strategies, replacement of fossil heating systems with heat pumps, electric vehicle social leasing and purchase subsidies, and public transport vouchers. Their distributional impacts, effectiveness in alleviating ETS2 burdens, greenhouse gas reduction potential, and cost effectiveness are compared across Member States. By jointly assessing distributional and environmental outcomes, the paper contributes to the design of socially fair and efficient climate policy packages and provides decision-makers relevant evidence to support the strategic use of SCF resources alongside the implementation of ETS2. Read the full abstract. Download presentation.

title: East Asian heatwaves intensify faster than they dissipate in a warming climate
summary: Abstract Extreme heat research has primarily emphasized static characteristics, while the temporal evolution of heatwaves remains less explored. Using observations (1979–2024) and CMIP6 simulations, we quantify heatwave lifecycle dynamics a
content: Abstract Extreme heat research has primarily emphasized static characteristics, while the temporal evolution of heatwaves remains less explored. Using observations (1979–2024) and CMIP6 simulations, we quantify heatwave lifecycle dynamics across East Asia in terms of onset and decay rates. Heatwaves consistently intensify faster than they dissipate, with stronger asymmetry at higher latitudes. Future changes depend strongly on how extremes are defined. Under a fixed-baseline framework, both onset and decay rates increase with warming, primarily associated with increasing peak temperatures. In contrast, using a moving baseline substantially reduces these increases in mid-latitudes, demonstrating that projected heatwave lifecycle changes are sensitive to the evolving climate reference state and may involve changes in climate variability and atmospheric circulation processes. These results highlight the importance of the climate reference framework when interpreting how heatwave lifecycle characteristics may change under continued warming.

title: Evaluating the Protection of Biodiversity and Environmental Resources under Saudi Environmental Law in Light of the Convention on Biological Diversity
summary: In light of the significant rate at which global biodiversity is declining, the necessity of reinforcing the legal frameworks for transferring international environmental commitments into practical national mechanisms has become pressing. T
content: In light of the significant rate at which global biodiversity is declining, the necessity of reinforcing the legal frameworks for transferring international environmental commitments into practical national mechanisms has become pressing. The Convention on Biological Diversity (CBD) serves as the international umbrella for biodiversity protection. Moreover, the effective application of the CBD is conditioned by the incorporation of its principles into domestic legislation. The purpose of this study was to verify the applicability of the CBD's preventive principles outlined in Article 14 to Saudi Environmental Law, especially Articles 6, 7, and 8 thereof, and to compare and correlate these two international and national systems. A doctrinal comparative legal analysis was undertaken to compare and correlate Article 14 of the CBD with the corresponding provisions of the Saudi Environmental Law through the application of analytical criteria for legal harmonization, consisting of preventive regulation, environmental risk management, resource governance, compliance enforcement systems, monitoring, accountability, and remediation of environmental harm. It has been concluded that there is a high degree of alignment between the CBD and Saudi Environmental Law; Article 14 of the CBD provides general procedural rules for preserving biodiversity, whereas Saudi Environmental Law Articles 6, 7, and 8 embody these principles in enforcement-oriented mechanisms. Finally, the paper recommends the internationalization of biodiversity governance and provides some recommendations for experience exchange on effective legislative practices. The study also advocates empirical research for further assessment of effective implementation and measurable biodiversity conservation outcomes.

title: Forever Young? On the technological impact of green startups
summary: We study the technological impact of inventions developed by firms operating in the green domain at an early stage of their lifecycle, Green Technology-Based Startups (GTBSs). Building on a large dataset of US patenting firms from 1976 to 2
content: We study the technological impact of inventions developed by firms operating in the green domain at an early stage of their lifecycle, Green Technology-Based Startups (GTBSs). Building on a large dataset of US patenting firms from 1976 to 2019, we compare the inventive performance of GTBSs with that of other startups and incumbent firms. We find that GTBSs develop inventions with higher impact compared to the other groups. This premium is concentrated in green technologies, it is strongest among firms that develop both green and non-green technologies and it is limited in time. It declines as firms mature, consistent with the consolidation of organizational routines over the firm lifecycle. Inventor-team technological distance is found to be central: GTBSs exhibit inventor-team distance comparable to other startups but exceeding that of incumbents, indicating that the inventions with the highest impact is generated at intermediate levels of cognitive diversity. Our results suggest that firm type, lifecycle dynamics and knowledge recombination jointly shape technological impact of GTBSs. We conclude that policies supporting startups that integrate green and non-green capabilities are more likely to yield higher inventive returns.

title: The rise of low-carbon industrialism: how the world economy is reconfigured through production, regulation, and space
summary: This article conceptualises low-carbon industrialism as a conceptual tool for studying the emerging planning order through which capitalism is being reorganised. While scholarship on green industrial policy has shown how states use regulati
content: This article conceptualises low-carbon industrialism as a conceptual tool for studying the emerging planning order through which capitalism is being reorganised. While scholarship on green industrial policy has shown how states use regulation to align climate goals with competitiveness, it often treats production, labour, regulation, and space in partial ways. I argue that a broader framework is needed to theorise how these dimensions are reconfigured together. The concept of low-carbon industrialism thus provides a framework for understanding a new accumulation regime and the uneven spatial, labour, and regulatory transformations reshaping the world economy.This process is transforming the hierarchies between core and peripheral regions of the world economy and is driven by a myriad of actors, including labour unions and mining firms. Therefore, we need to understand these multiscalar processes as unfolding, relational, and contingent. Hence, this article calls for three analytical moves: first, overcoming Cartesian dualism and paying attention to working-class environmentalism; second, adopting a socio-legal approach to understand lawfare; and third, understanding low-carbon industrialism as a global, relational process by scrutinising the regulatory power and productive capacity of regions.

title: Bio-inspired Quasi-periodic Photonic Structure for Highper-formance Passive Radiative Heating
summary: Abstract The operational performance of equipment is often significantly compromised in low-temperature environments, posing serious threats to the reliability of critical infrastructure and other key sectors. Meanwhile, global climate gove
content: Abstract The operational performance of equipment is often significantly compromised in low-temperature environments, posing serious threats to the reliability of critical infrastructure and other key sectors. Meanwhile, global climate governance initiatives have mandated urgent reductions in greenhouse gas emissions. Consequently, the high carbon footprint associated with conventional thermal management technologies conflicts with climate mitigation goals, underscoring the need to develop passive thermal management solutions. Passive radiative heating technology enables net heat gain in low-temperature environments by efficiently absorbing solar radiation and suppressing thermal emission in the mid-infrared band. In this work, we integrate quasi-periodic sequences with a biomimetic diatom frustule structure to propose a new passive radiative heating configuration. The designed structure achieves a visible-band (0.4-0.7 μm) average absorptance of over 95%, and an AM 1.5 solar-weighted integrated absorptance of 89.72% across the full solar spectrum (0.3-2.5 μm), and low emissivity within the atmospheric window, ultimately realizing a net radiative heating power exceeding 410 W/m². Moreover, the structure also exhibits high angular stability, maintaining an average solar absorptance above 85% even at a 60° incidence angle. Furthermore, the structure exhibits robust stabilization against material parameter variations, showing negligible decay in overall absorptance even after significant changes in material parameters. These results indicate that the proposed biomimetic passive radiative heating structure offers a viable solution for addressing low-temperature operational challenges and supporting carbon neutrality objectives.

title: Single-level MILP incentive pricing for customer directrix load-based demand response in smart buildings
summary: Introduction With the high penetration of renewable energy, tapping the regulation potential of smart buildings in distribution networks plays a pivotal role in enabling orderly renewable energy accommodation. Customer directrix load-based
content: Introduction With the high penetration of renewable energy, tapping the regulation potential of smart buildings in distribution networks plays a pivotal role in enabling orderly renewable energy accommodation. Customer directrix load-based demand response serves as an effective mechanism for guiding smart building interaction. However, its incentive price, derived as the equilibrium point of a leader-follower game between the operator and load entities, relies on a corresponding bilevel optimization model that suffers from low computational efficiency. Methods To address this limitation, an efficient incentive pricing method is proposed. The proposed linear similarity metric and incentive revenue formulation ensure the linearity of the lower-level optimization problem. Subsequently, based on primal-dual feasibility, an aggregated strong-duality equality, and a discrete-price reformulation, the original bilevel model is accurately reformulated into a single-level mixed-integer linear programming problem, enabling a one-shot determination of the incentive price. Results Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed linear metric is highly consistent with traditional nonlinear metrics in terms of ranking monotonicity. Compared with time-of-use-only demand response and fixed incentive pricing strategies, the proposed method can identify an economically balanced incentive price that effectively guides smart building energy consumption behavior, improves renewable energy accommodation, and maintains favorable economic performance for both the distribution system operator and smart buildings. Discussion These findings support the use of the proposed single-level MILP framework for balancing renewable energy accommodation with the economic interests of the distribution system operator and smart buildings.

title: High‐Value Utilization of Typical Vanadium‐Bearing Solid Wastes: Mineralogy, Pathways, and Perspectives
summary: ABSTRACT Vanadium‐bearing solid wastes (VBSWs) have emerged as a key research priority in resource recovery and environmental remediation because of their high resource value, large generation volume, and complex phase composition. However,
content: ABSTRACT Vanadium‐bearing solid wastes (VBSWs) have emerged as a key research priority in resource recovery and environmental remediation because of their high resource value, large generation volume, and complex phase composition. However, practical utilization of these wastes still faces major challenges, including heavy environmental burdens, ill‐suited recycling technologies, and a low rate of high‐value utilization. Therefore, the development of efficient and environmentally friendly treatment technologies is crucial for securing vanadium supply, promoting the sustainable development of the vanadium industry, and achieving carbon peak and neutrality goals. This study systematically summarizes the process mineralogical characteristics of four typical VBSWs: vanadium‐titanium magnetite tailings (VTMTs), vanadium slag, spent vanadium catalysts, and vanadium‐containing sludge. It focuses on reviewing current technologies and their practical applications for the synergistic utilization and high‐value conversion of components in these wastes. Additionally, the study analyzes existing technical bottlenecks and proposes optimization pathways, aiming to provide a scientific basis for the targeted, green, and efficient utilization of VBSWs and to guide advancement toward cleaner, higher‐value development. Finally, future directions for high‐value utilization technologies are proposed to further promote the treatment and resource recovery of VBSWs.

title: Upcycled Food Research for Sustainable Food System Transition: Analysis of Global Trends, Korean Market Status, and Applicability
source: Journal of the Korean Society of Food Science and Nutrition
