title: Advances in mitochondrial compartmentalization for terpenoid synthesis in Saccharomyces cerevisiae
summary: Mitochondria provide a unique enriched acetyl coenzyme A reservoir and an ideal redox environment, offering an efficient supply for the biosynthesis of terpene precursors and terpene products. This comprehensive review focuses on the engine
content: Mitochondria provide a unique enriched acetyl coenzyme A reservoir and an ideal redox environment, offering an efficient supply for the biosynthesis of terpene precursors and terpene products. This comprehensive review focuses on the engineering of mitochondrial compartmentalization in Saccharomyces cerevisiae to enhance terpene production. We systematically outline the applications from hemiterpenes to tetraterpenes and elaborate on how advanced strategies, such as key enzyme mitochondrial targeting strategy, whole-pathway mitochondrial targeting strategy, dual cytoplasmic-mitochondrial compartmentalization strategy, and multi-organelle synergistic compartmentalization strategy, can effectively improve precursor availability while mitigating metabolic interference and cytotoxic effects. In addition, we critically examine the discussions and long-term challenges associated with these methods. Finally, we highlight the transformative potential of mitochondrial compartmentalization to pioneer future innovations in complex terpene synthesis engineering.

title: Educating Future Engineers to be Responsible Citizens
summary: In a time of rapid technological and societal transformation, universities are called upon to prepare future engineers not only for professional success, but also for their societal responsibilities. In addition to technical expertise, engi
content: In a time of rapid technological and societal transformation, universities are called upon to prepare future engineers not only for professional success, but also for their societal responsibilities. In addition to technical expertise, engineers need ethical awareness, sustainability competencies, and the ability to reflect critically on the consequences of their actions. Topics such as digitalization, artificial intelligence, and data literacy are becoming increasingly essential. Engineering education must therefore integrate socially relevant skills alongside scientific and methodological foundations. This article presents the ongoing transformation of engineering curricula at TU Berlin, beginning with the adoption of a mission statement on teaching in 2018. It outlines key developments over the past six years, including structural measures and teaching formats designed to foster ethics, sustainability, and interdisciplinary thinking. Practical examples demonstrate how these topics can be embedded into existing programs through interdisciplinary collaboration and curriculum development. The article also reflects on obstacles encountered and lessons learned along the way. By sharing these insights, it aims to contribute to the international dialogue on engineering education and invites readers to discuss strategies, methods, and structures that support the development of responsible and socially engaged engineers. Keywords: Sustainability, ethics, data literacy, responsible citizens, curriculum development

title: From straw burning to incorporation: climate risk and farm machineries availability catalyse sustainable behavioural change among rice farmers
summary: Abstract Open burning of rice straw remains widespread across many rice-producing regions, generating avoidable greenhouse gas emissions, air pollution, and soil degradation. Yet the transition to sustainable straw management remains limite
content: Abstract Open burning of rice straw remains widespread across many rice-producing regions, generating avoidable greenhouse gas emissions, air pollution, and soil degradation. Yet the transition to sustainable straw management remains limited, especially in climate-stressed smallholder systems. This study explores farmers’ behavioral readiness and economic preferences to adopt rice-straw incorporation, willingness to pay (WTP) for its adoption, and identifies how socioeconomic, farm and climatic factors shaping these decisions. Using a combination of contingent valuation method, ordered logit, Heckman selection, and double-hurdle models, we analyze survey data of 435 rice-farmers collected through stratified-random sampling from three climate-hazardous (i.e., drought, salinity, and flood) districts and one less climate-risk district of Bangladesh. Adoption of straw-incorporation is very low (14%), however, a larger share of farmers (31%) show interest in adopting and 28% are willing to pay an average of USD37/ha/season—revealing substantial latent demand for straw-incorporation. Farmers in climate-vulnerable areas show a significantly higher probability of paying for straw-incorporation than those in less vulnerable areas, with WTP highest in salinity-affected regions. The finding implies that climate risk acts as a catalyst for behavioral change toward adoption of sustainable straw-management. Education, household income and accessibility to farm-machineries are the key drivers of shifting towards straw-incorporation and its WTP. Given Bangladesh’s dependence on rental farm machinery, subsidized and accessible straw-management machinery rental services could enable adoption at costs below farmers stated WTP. These findings provide globally relevant evidence that climate risk can increase receptiveness to low-emission residue management in smallholder rice systems. For climate-vulnerable and resource-constrained agricultural economies, the results suggest targeted machinery access, increasing farmer’s awareness, and market-based incentives such as carbon finance to accelerate the shift from open burning to sustainable straw management.

title: Effectiveness of a Natural Fertilizer from Organic Household Waste (Banana Peel, Orange Peel, Eggshell, and Onion Peel) versus Chemical Fertilizer on The Growth of Chili (Capsicum Annuum L.): A Comparative Analysis
summary: Commercial chemical fertilizers are heavily relied upon to boost crop yields, but their rising costs and negative environmental impacts—such as soil degradation and water contamination—highlight the critical need for sustainable alternative
content: Commercial chemical fertilizers are heavily relied upon to boost crop yields, but their rising costs and negative environmental impacts—such as soil degradation and water contamination—highlight the critical need for sustainable alternatives. This study evaluated the effectiveness of a liquid natural fertilizer formulated from organic household wastes, including banana peels, orange peels, eggshells, onion peels, rice wash water, and molasses, on the growth performance of chili (Capsicum annuum L.) plants. Utilizing an experimental research design, chili seedlings were divided into four groups to compare the organic formulation (at 5 mL and 10 mL concentrations) against a commercial synthetic fertilizer and a water-only control group. The plants were monitored over an eight-day treatment period using two primary metrics: plant height and leaf count. The results demonstrated that the organic formulation is highly effective in promoting key growth parameters. In terms of plant height, the water-only control group achieved the highest average height of 8.6 inches, followed closely by the 10 mL organic fertilizer group at 8.1 inches, while both the chemical fertilizer and 5 mL organic treatments recorded the shortest height at 7.7 inches. Conversely, in the metric of leaf production, the 10 mL organic fertilizer concentration demonstrated the strongest performance, yielding the highest average of 10.6 leaves. The water-only and 5 mL organic groups resulted in 8.4 leaves, whereas the chemical fertilizer group performed the worst, recording the lowest average of 4.2 leaves. These findings confirm that the homemade organic fertilizer can rival and surpass commercial options, particularly in supporting leaf growth. The study concludes that recycling household kitchen waste into a liquid biofertilizer provides a practical, eco-friendly, and cost-effective solution for sustainable urban agriculture.

title: Distribution of Minerals and Some Heavy Metals in the Leaves and Stems of Salvia, Ziziphus, Thyme, and Artemisia Plants
summary: Depending on the species and the organ of the plant, medicinal and aromatic plants can vary significantly in their mineral make-up. This experiment compared sodium (Na), potassium (K), iron (Fe), zinc (Zn), copper (Cu), and manganese (Mn) i
content: Depending on the species and the organ of the plant, medicinal and aromatic plants can vary significantly in their mineral make-up. This experiment compared sodium (Na), potassium (K), iron (Fe), zinc (Zn), copper (Cu), and manganese (Mn) in the leaves and stems of Salvia, Ziziphus, thyme and Artemisia growing in the Al-Jabal Al-Akhdar region of Libya in spring 2024. Measurement of sodium and potassium was done by flame photometry, and Fe, Zn, Cu, and Mn by atomic absorption spectrometry, after acid digestion. The most common macro element in all the samples was potassium. It had a mean concentration of 4.98 ± 0.84 mg/g in leaves and 5.39 ± 1.20 mg/g in stems, versus 1.28 ± 1.09 and 0.897 ± 0.485 mg/g in sodium, respectively. The mean concentration of the trace elements in both organs had the same order: Mn > Zn > Cu > Fe. Artemisia leaves had the highest Na (2.84 mg/g), Zn (37.07 µg/g), Cu (15.09 µg/g) and Mn (66.39 µg/g) and Salvia leaves had the highest K concentration (5.57 mg/g). Artemisia had the highest K (6.53 mg/g), Zn (18.27 µg/g), and Cu (9.21 µg/g), Ziziphus the highest Mn (77.50 µg/g) and thyme the highest Fe (1.02 µg/g). The findings show apparent species- and organ-based variations in the distribution of elements. Since no analytical replicates, recovery, detection limits or certified reference-material results are reported in the dataset, the results should be considered as descriptive and cannot be used independently to determine dietary adequacy, toxicity, or safety.

title: Delay-consistent adaptive incentive governance for circular beverage packaging systems: distinguishing structural and algorithmic limits in PET and returnable glass recovery in Mexico
summary: Mexico's 2030 target of 80% PET-container recovery under the ANNEP agreement remains 16 percentage points above the current national recovery rate, with returnable glass already operating near its infrastructure asymptote. Whether adaptive
content: Mexico's 2030 target of 80% PET-container recovery under the ANNEP agreement remains 16 percentage points above the current national recovery rate, with returnable glass already operating near its infrastructure asymptote. Whether adaptive incentive governance can close this gap depends on distinguishing the mechanism sources of policy performance: the adaptive feedback timing itself, the average incentive intensity at which policies operate, or the underlying behavioral response of the recovery system. This paper investigates the distinction using a delay-consistent adaptive proportional–integral controller embedded in a system-dynamics closed-loop supply chain calibrated against four independent empirical sources for the Mexican beverage-container context. Four policies are compared in a 216-cell balanced factorial design: a no-incentive baseline, a constant deposit-refund, an adaptive proportional–integral controller, and a quarterly threshold rule. A new stratified matched-budget identification experiment decomposes policy performance into three analytically distinct levels — algorithmic effects, operating-point effects, and structural constraints — by comparing the adaptive controller against an equivalent-intensity fixed benchmark across baseline, demand-dip, and demand-whiplash regimes. The matched-budget analysis indicates that the adaptive controller and the equivalent-intensity fixed policy converge to essentially identical steady-state return rates (approximately 0.759) under all three demand regimes; the previously observed adaptive advantage is attributable to operating-point effects rather than to feedback timing. This identification supports interpreting the 2.1-percentage-point gap between the observed ceiling and the 0.78 composite target as structural rather than algorithmic in origin: the ceiling reflects the saturating Michaelis–Menten behavioral response of the recovery system, not a limitation of the control algorithm. Closing this gap requires policy instruments capable of expanding the behavioral elasticity envelope itself — reverse-vending densification, extended producer responsibility, informal-sector formalization, and consumer information campaigns — rather than stronger deposit-refund incentives alone. • Matched-budget identification experiment isolates algorithmic from operating-point effects in deposit-refund governance. • Adaptive controller and equivalent-intensity fixed policy converge to identical return rates across three demand regimes. • The 0.759 composite return-rate ceiling is structural, not algorithmic — reflecting behavioral elasticity limits. • Structural ceiling stops recovery 2.1 percentage points below Mexico's 0.78 composite target under current elasticities. • Closing the gap requires elasticity-envelope expansion, not stronger deposit-refund incentives.

title: Minor geographies of climate action: hedgerows, children’s storytelling and playful environmental participation
summary: Hedgerows are sometimes prickly, sometimes juicy, everyday features of the landscapes we walk past in daily life. Formed from shrubs, trees and other vegetation, they mark field boundaries, roadsides and gardens, while working as biodiversi
content: Hedgerows are sometimes prickly, sometimes juicy, everyday features of the landscapes we walk past in daily life. Formed from shrubs, trees and other vegetation, they mark field boundaries, roadsides and gardens, while working as biodiversity corridors, habitats, carbon stores, foraging spaces and allies in flood mitigation. Yet, because they are ordinary, local and easily overlooked, hedgerows rarely command the same public imagination as forests, rivers or charismatic wildlife.This paper challenges the idea of the hedgerow as mundane, reframing it as a lively actor in ecological diversity, cultural imagination and climate pedagogy. Drawing on a long-form Youth Participatory Action Research project with young people who named themselves the “HedgeHunters”, we explore the co-creation of the children’s storybook The Mystery of the Giant Claw. Through Hunter the Hedgehog, Twig the hedgerow and a multispecies cast, young people explored pollution, biodiversity loss, care and human behaviour. We show how playful co-creation can transform overlooked landscapes into sites of connection, creativity, environmental action and climate hope. We argue that hedgerows offer a “minor geography” through which young people can engage with climate change and environmental justice, and that playfulness is a serious mode of climate pedagogy supporting emotion, systems thinking and collective agency.

title: Greenwashing ESG: Tren Global atau Ilusi Keberlanjutan? Analisis Pengaruh Intellectual Capital dan ESG terhadap Nilai Perusahaan
summary: This study aims to analyze the influence of Intellectual Capital (IC) and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure on firm value in the consumer non-cyclical sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the perio
content: This study aims to analyze the influence of Intellectual Capital (IC) and Environmental, Social, and Governance (ESG) disclosure on firm value in the consumer non-cyclical sector listed on the Indonesia Stock Exchange (IDX) during the period 2022–2025. The research is motivated by the growing importance of intangible assets and sustainability practices in shaping market perceptions, particularly in industries characterized by high competition and strong reliance on innovation. Firm value is measured using the Price to Earnings Ratio (PER), which is considered to better reflect market expectations of profitability compared to Tobin’s Q or Price to Book Value. A quantitative approach was employed with purposive sampling of 76 firm-year observations and multiple regression analysis to determine the appropriate model. The findings reveal that IC has a significant positive effect on firm value, confirming that efficiency in managing human capital, structural capital, and relational capital enhances investor confidence and long-term growth prospects. In contrast, ESG disclosure shows a significant negative effect, indicating that the market has not yet perceived sustainability reporting as a positive signal, but rather as an additional cost that reduces short-term profitability. This result strengthens the indication of greenwashing practices due to weak ESG reporting standards in Indonesia. The coefficient of determination (R²) of 0.612 demonstrates that IC and ESG jointly explain more than half of the variation in firm value. This study contributes theoretically by emphasizing the dominant role of IC as a determinant of firm value in emerging markets and practically by providing implications for management, investors, and regulators in addressing the dilemma of whether ESG represents a global trend or merely an illusion of sustainability.

title: Beyond green buildings: circular economy strategies and SDG alignment in India's urban housing sector
summary: The circular economy (CE) within the construction sector has gained interest from both practitioners and policymakers. However, its acceptance lags behind other sustainability-related concepts such as energy efficiency and green buildings (
content: The circular economy (CE) within the construction sector has gained interest from both practitioners and policymakers. However, its acceptance lags behind other sustainability-related concepts such as energy efficiency and green buildings (GB), especially in countries in the Global South. Although CE directly aligns with the sustainable development goals (SDGs), there is no explicit reference to CE within the SDG framework or vice versa. Understanding how practitioners in the Global South view CE principles in the construction sector and how those principles align with the different SDGs is therefore vital. This is especially the case in the post-pandemic era, where building usage has changed amid major disruptions to global supply chains. This paper analyses data from a focus group of construction sector practitioners in India to understand how CE principles can be adopted within the residential construction sector and how, in turn, they may contribute to achieving the SDGs. The findings show that practitioner-derived CE interventions were primarily framed around resource efficiency, low-carbon materials, clean energy, GB performance, and construction and demolition waste. Although participants primarily associated these interventions with an environmental orientation, target-level analysis revealed wider potential links with health, employment, urban resilience, institutional capacity, and partnerships. The outcomes also highlighted a persistent conceptual overlap between CE and GB thinking, with limited emphasis on higher-order circular strategies and systemic value retention. This illustrates that the construction industry needs to move beyond traditional GB paradigms towards a more holistic, systems-based approach to sustainability. The paper highlights the need for policy coherence, professional capacity building, multi-stakeholder collaboration, and technological innovation to better align CE strategies with the SDGs, especially in the Global South, where socio-economic priorities remain central.

title: The everyday forests we don’t see in official reports: A conceptual shift for socially just forestry
summary: Forestry is commonly framed through biophysical metrics - canopy cover, timber yields, carbon stocks - defined by global standards that travel into national policies. These definitions frequently displace the lived landscapes in which fores
content: Forestry is commonly framed through biophysical metrics - canopy cover, timber yields, carbon stocks - defined by global standards that travel into national policies. These definitions frequently displace the lived landscapes in which forests are sustained. This perspective article argues for a conceptual shift: recognizing the everyday work of care and organizing - often unpaid, often feminized, that bring into being and sustain forest landscapes - as central to forest governance. Drawing on research across the Global South and North, I show how technocratic forest definitions and program architectures overlook social reproduction, spiritual values, and affective ties, thereby fueling conflict, eroding legitimacy, and weakening outcomes. I propose an agenda for just forestry that (i) values care work in forests and communities, (ii) recognizes informal organizing in decision-making, (iii) embraces plural values associated with forestry, and (iv) adopts a systemic lens that entails coordination with sectors beyond forestry as well as across scales, from local governance to international climate programs. Reframing forests as lived landscapes - entangled with everyday practices, identities, and relationships - does more than correct blind spots - it offers practical pathways for durable stewardship under climate and biodiversity crises.

title: Biodiversity-inclusive insurance for supply chains: Assessing positive ecological impacts through a novel MCDM method
summary: Global supply chains face increasing disruptions due to biodiversity loss, which undermines vital ecosystem services such as climate regulation, water management and pollination. Despite this growing risk, traditional insurance models often
content: Global supply chains face increasing disruptions due to biodiversity loss, which undermines vital ecosystem services such as climate regulation, water management and pollination. Despite this growing risk, traditional insurance models often fail to incorporate ecological dimensions, limiting their effectiveness in mitigating the vulnerability of supply chains to ecological changes. This study addresses this gap by developing a structured framework for evaluating insurance models that explicitly consider biodiversity-related risks. The primary contribution lies in the definition of four novel biodiversity-focused insurance models, Biodiversity-Linked Insurance (BLI), Ecosystem-Based Insurance (EBI), Parametric Biodiversity Risk Insurance (PBRI), and Supply Chain Disruption Insurance for Biodiversity Risks (SCDI-BR), and the establishment of twelve comprehensive criteria spanning ecological, financial, operational, and regulatory dimensions. To support model selection, the study introduces a novel multi-criteria decision-making method, the Asymmetric Linear Evaluation using Cosine Similarity Approach (ALECSA), which integrates asymmetric stakeholder preferences and penalty factors. Criteria weights were determined using the Best-Worst Method based on expert evaluations across logistics, insurance, biodiversity and policy sectors. The application of the proposed framework identified EBI as the most effective model, followed by BLI, PBRI and SCDI-BR, and the findings were validated using established MCDM techniques, confirming the robustness of results. Several criteria function as ecological indicators that reflect positive biodiversity impacts, such as risk reduction, alignment with sustainability goals and proactive ecological practices, underscoring the importance of embedding biodiversity considerations into supply chain risk management under climate stress.

title: Phosphorus efficiency in soybean genotypes: investigating morphological and physiological plant traits
summary: Abstract This study aimed to (i) classify soybean genotypes related to P uptake and utilization efficiencies and responsiveness to P supply; (ii) investigate plant morphological and physiological characteristics related to P efficiencies; a
content: Abstract This study aimed to (i) classify soybean genotypes related to P uptake and utilization efficiencies and responsiveness to P supply; (ii) investigate plant morphological and physiological characteristics related to P efficiencies; and (iii) identify plant traits for selecting P–efficient genotypes. Sixteen soybean genotypes grew under deficient and sufficient P supply (10 and 100 µmol P L − 1 ). Phosphorus absorption kinetic parameters, root morphology, growth, photosynthetic, and nutritional parameters were determined to investigate the P acquisition efficiency (PAE) and P utilization efficiency (PUE). Soybean genotypes with high PAE exhibited a twofold greater P influx, and approximately 25% lower values of both the Michaelis–Menten constant (K m ) and the minimum solution concentration at which influx ceases (C min ) compared to low–PAE genotypes. Specifically, K m values decreased from 0.66 to 0.68 in low-PAE genotypes to 0.52–0.59 in high–PAE genotypes, while C min values decreased from 0.80 to 0.86 to 0.65–0.78, respectively. Genotypes with high PUE showed higher rates of net photosynthesis and electron transport, and leaf area, associated with lower light stress than low PUE genotypes. Only one soybean genotype (BMX 50i52 IPRO) was efficient in both acquisition and utilization of P, as well as responsive to P application. Leaf area may represent a promising trait for the initial screening of P-efficient soybean genotypes, although validation under soil and field conditions is still required. Our findings provide foundational knowledge for bioengineering soybean P–efficient genotypes, possibly assisting in reducing the overall reliance on P fertilization even more relevant under P impoverished environments.

title: Beyond access: Evaluating adoption and utilisation of solar energy in unserved and underserved communities in Northern Nigeria
source: Energy Sustainable Development/Energy for sustainable development
summary: Expanding electricity access through decentralised renewable energy systems has become a central strategy for achieving universal energy access in developing countries. However, evaluations of decentralised rural electrification have largel
content: Expanding electricity access through decentralised renewable energy systems has become a central strategy for achieving universal energy access in developing countries. However, evaluations of decentralised rural electrification have largely focused on infrastructure deployment and electricity access, with limited attention to what occurs after electricity becomes available. This study demonstrates that evaluating decentralised rural electrification requires moving beyond conventional measures of electricity access to consider whether available energy services are subsequently adopted and effectively utilised. Accordingly, a post-access analytical perspective was adopted to evaluate the adoption and utilisation of decentralised solar energy technologies among solar energy users in Rural Electrification Agency (REA)-supported unserved and underserved communities in Northern Nigeria. A cross-sectional community-based survey was conducted among 484 solar energy users across 38 REA-supported intervention communities in six northern Nigerian states. A Probit regression model was employed to identify the factors associated with solar energy adoption, while descriptive statistics were used to assess sectoral utilisation patterns. The results show that adoption was significantly associated with knowledge of solar energy, training, affordability, occupation, duration and intensity of use, perceived importance of solar energy, and sources of information, whereas education level and geographical location were not independently associated with adoption. Solar energy was utilised across residential, commercial, social, industrial, and institutional sectors, with commercial and residential activities accounting for the largest share of utilisation. Solar energy was utilised across residential, commercial, social, industrial, and institutional sectors, with commercial and residential activities accounting for the largest share of utilisation, including applications such as small business operations ranging from mobile phone charging, barbing, cold storage, to irrigation. By integrating technology adoption and utilisation within a single post-access analytical perspective, this study provides a more comprehensive framework for evaluating the effectiveness of decentralised rural electrification programmes. The findings offer practical evidence to support policymakers and programme implementers in strengthening the design, monitoring, and long-term sustainability of decentralised rural electrification interventions in Nigeria and other developing countries.

title: OsDUF3615 regulates grain size and quality traits by modulating cell proliferation and starch metabolism in rice
summary: Domains of Unknown Function (DUFs) are widely distributed across diverse genomes and are increasingly recognized as important regulators of plant growth, development, and stress responses. DUF3615 is a highly conserved plant-specific protei
content: Domains of Unknown Function (DUFs) are widely distributed across diverse genomes and are increasingly recognized as important regulators of plant growth, development, and stress responses. DUF3615 is a highly conserved plant-specific protein motif; however, its biological function remains largely unknown. Previously, the gene OsGAPC3 , a key regulator of grain quality, was isolated and functionally characterized in rice. Transcriptome analysis during the dissection of the OsGAPC3 -mediated regulatory pathway revealed that OsDUF3615 is significantly upregulated in Osgapc3 mutants, suggesting its potential involvement in rice development and grain traits. In this study, we show that OsDUF3615 is constitutively expressed in rice and encodes a nucleus-localized protein. Functional analysis demonstrated that overexpression of OsDUF3615 significantly promotes cell proliferation and expansion in the lemma along the grain width axis, leading to increased grain width and thousand-grain weight. Moreover, OsDUF3615 modulates grain filling dynamics and alters the accumulation of major storage compounds, including starch and free fatty acids, thereby affecting both nutritional composition and eating quality traits, such as taste value. Collectively, our findings identify OsDUF3615 as a key regulator of rice grain development and quality formation, providing valuable genetic resources for the molecular breeding of high-quality rice varieties.

title: Improving cost competitiveness in hydrogen production pathways through technology maturity, patent concentration and game-theoretic classification
summary: Many hydrogen projects face cancellation due to high development costs and contractual asymmetries between technology licensors and project developers, highlighting the need for strategic frameworks to enhance efficient collaborations. This
content: Many hydrogen projects face cancellation due to high development costs and contractual asymmetries between technology licensors and project developers, highlighting the need for strategic frameworks to enhance efficient collaborations. This study employs a multi-method approach based on a Systematic Literature Review (SLR) and analytical classification. The approach extends the Kraljic matrix to innovation-intensive technologies. Technology Readiness Levels (TRLs) and market growth are used as proxies for profit impact, while the Herfindahl–Hirschman Index (HHI) measures supply risk through patent concentration. Hydrogen production pathways are then classified and linked to cooperative and non-cooperative game-theoretic models to evaluate optimal collaboration strategies between licensors and project developers. Our analysis shows that non-cooperative models dominate when technologies exhibit low-to-medium technology maturity and smaller market growth, such as Solid Oxide Electrolysis Cell (SOEC), Anion-Exchange Membrane electrolysis (AEM), or Turquoise technology process. A mix of cooperative and non-cooperative games is included in Strategic contexts, such as Proton-Exchange Membrane (PEM) electrolysis, Alkaline Water Electrolysis (AWE) green hydrogen, grey and blue hydrogen technology process, where patent complementarities and balanced bargaining power foster joint innovation. The proposed classification offers a structured pathway to bridge procurement strategy, market structure and innovation governance in the hydrogen sector, and it helps project developers to identify which technologies carry higher HHI, which game-theoretic strategy should be applied to achieve more effective cooperative outcomes. The results directly support hydrogen developers in selecting technologies and reducing sourcing risk.

title: Examining the Extent of ESG Practices of Nigerian Money-Deposit Banking Sector In S&P Global Rating
source: IIARD INTERNATIONAL JOURNAL OF BANKING AND FINANCE RESEARCH
summary: The alienation of banks from ESG practices requirement in many quarters has made the study of ESG practices as relate to banking sector an interesting one. This serves as the backdrop for the aim of this study - to examine the extent of ESG
content: The alienation of banks from ESG practices requirement in many quarters has made the study of ESG practices as relate to banking sector an interesting one. This serves as the backdrop for the aim of this study - to examine the extent of ESG practices of money-deposit banks in Nigeria featured in S&P Global. Conceptual, empirical and theoretical reviews/framework were provided to support the study. Quantitative and descriptive designs employed ensured that ESG quantitative data/scores for Nigerian Money-deposit banks in S&P Global’s ESG scores(used as the dependent variables), and its respective ESC industry average (used as the independent), were retrieved. These data were analyzed using Independent Sample T-test in SPSS statistics (ver. 25) so to ascertain if a statistically significant difference in mean exist between the ESG breakdown scores of the sampled banks and their industry average. From the outcome, it was revealed that no statistically significant difference in mean exist between the ESG breakdown scores of selected banks (Zenith bank plc and UBA plc) and their industry-averages. That is, both banks fared impressively in recent times, with respect of ESG sustainable practices when compared to the ESG industry-averages. However, with great deficit in ESG overall score of the aforementioned banks, when compared to their counterparts in advanced countries of the world, indicates that there are areas of improvement in their ESG sustainable practices. Sequel to this, it was recommended that greater utilization of alternative and cleaner energy-sources and technologies by Nigerian moneydeposit banks to consolidate on their green banking practices (GBP) particularly in reducing scope 1 & 2 emissions. More also, a sector-wide ESG-related regulations and policies should be developed and enforced in Nigeria to promote the standardization of ESG practices and regulatory-driven GBP.

title: Industrial Policy for China's Strategic Emerging Industries From the Perspective of New Structural Economics
summary: ABSTRACT Against global industrial restructuring and fiercer tech competition, strategic emerging industries (SEIs) serve as China's core engine to develop new‐quality productive forces, overcome high‐end tech bottlenecks, and advance high‐
content: ABSTRACT Against global industrial restructuring and fiercer tech competition, strategic emerging industries (SEIs) serve as China's core engine to develop new‐quality productive forces, overcome high‐end tech bottlenecks, and advance high‐quality growth. Drawing on New Structural Economics, this paper analyzes the evolutionary logic, effects, and optimization paths of China's SEI industrial policies. We find that the effective industrial policies for SEIs should follow the dynamic change of factor endowment structure and adapt to local conditions and time conditions as the key bottlenecks for industrial upgrading change. The study also shows that for industries tied to national defense and economic security, industrial policies should seek a reasonable balance between efficiency and security. Finally, we propose that China's industrial policies for SEIs should shift from extensive subsidy‐oriented intervention to precise, market‐oriented, and efficiency‐driven governance, supporting sustainable high‐quality SEI growth and national industrial transformation.

title: The Uncertain Making of Law: Controversies and Political Framings Around Cellular Meat in France
summary: Abstract Cellular meat is at the centre of a growing socio-technical controversy in France. While it is promoted as a sustainable alternative to conventional meat, its regulation raises political, legal and ethical challenges. Taking a soci
content: Abstract Cellular meat is at the centre of a growing socio-technical controversy in France. While it is promoted as a sustainable alternative to conventional meat, its regulation raises political, legal and ethical challenges. Taking a socio-legal and pragmatic approach, this article examines how socio-technical controversies expressed in public debates and institutional framings shape the emerging regulatory framework. It sheds light on the mechanisms through which certain voices and concerns are amplified in the legislative process, while others remain marginalised. Drawing on documentary research, interviews and French parliamentary debates on cellular meat, the study shows how law operates as a site of negotiation where competing values and interests are translated into norms. By examining the case of cellular meat, the article emphasises the importance of understanding law not as a fixed set of rules, but as a living practice shaped by controversies, narratives and power relations. Taken together, this perspective offers valuable insights into the challenges of regulating emerging food technologies in complex and plural societies, and highlights the need for inclusive and context-sensitive regulation.

title: Loss of MAX1 redirects, rather than delays, the leaf senescence program in lettuce
summary: Background Strigolactones (SLs) regulate diverse aspects of plant development and have been implicated in promoting leaf senescence. However, senescence phenotypes associated with SL deficiency have not been consistently observed across spe
content: Background Strigolactones (SLs) regulate diverse aspects of plant development and have been implicated in promoting leaf senescence. However, senescence phenotypes associated with SL deficiency have not been consistently observed across species, suggesting that this function may be species- or context-dependent. Moreover, the contribution of endogenous SL biosynthesis to senescence in leafy vegetable crops remains unclear. Here, we investigated the role of the SL biosynthetic gene MORE AXILLARY GROWTH1 (MAX1) in dark-induced leaf senescence in lettuce (Lactuca sativa). Results We found that endogenous SL biosynthesis plays a major role in dark-induced senescence in lettuce. SL pathway genes were induced during dark storage, while exogenous GR24 accelerated senescence and lettuce MAX1 (LsMAX1) complemented the delayed-senescence phenotype of the Arabidopsis max1 mutant. Consistent with these findings, CRISPR/Cas9-generated Lsmax1 mutants exhibited a pronounced stay-green phenotype during prolonged darkness, accompanied by strongly reduced induction of key senescence-associated genes. Despite this delayed visible senescence, Lsmax1 retained a substantial transcriptional response to dark storage. Strikingly, loss of LsMAX1 did not simply weaken the wild-type senescence program, but redirected part of the response toward a distinct stress-associated transcriptional state that was largely absent from wild type. Loss of LsMAX1 did not affect vegetative rosette architecture, although increased branching emerged after bolting. Conclusions Our findings establish MAX1-dependent SL biosynthesis as an important regulator of leaf senescence in lettuce and reveal a role that extends beyond controlling the rate of senescence. Rather than simply delaying the wild-type program, loss of LsMAX1 alters the transcriptional trajectory of senescence, favoring an alternative stress-associated state during prolonged darkness. The strong stay-green phenotype without detectable changes to vegetative rosette architecture further highlights SL biosynthesis as a potential target for extending postharvest longevity in lettuce and other leafy crops.

title: Research on the Hybrid Design of Children’s Toys and Stationery for Sustainable Consumption
summary: In order to cope with the common functional fragmentation, short product lifespan and serious waste of resources in children's stationery and toys, this study proposes a sustainable design method for children's products through SnapPen desi
content: In order to cope with the common functional fragmentation, short product lifespan and serious waste of resources in children's stationery and toys, this study proposes a sustainable design method for children's products through SnapPen designed by the author. SnapPen is a hybrid product that integrates watercolor pens and blocks. The study combines the principle of circular economy with product lifespan extension strategies to promote sustainable consumption. By integrating user behavior analysis, modular structure design and material sustainability evaluation, the study establishes a design framework centered on functional transformation, emotional attachment and recycling. Design practice shows that the hybrid design strategy can not only realize multi-functional use to extend the physical lifespan of the product, but also strengthen the emotional bond through the active participation of children in the assembly and conversion process, thus greatly reducing the intention of discarding. This article systematically discusses the concept of sustainable design, existing problems, design strategies and practical verification, and provides an applicable reference model for the sustainable design of children's products.

title: Polyurethane nanocomposite film embedded with carbon quantum dots from spent Coffea arabica grounds for the UV and blue light shielding
summary: The development of anti-blue-light coatings simultaneously possessing high optical transparency and blue-light protective functions derived from renewable and biodegradable biomass represents a promising strategy for eye protection. In the
content: The development of anti-blue-light coatings simultaneously possessing high optical transparency and blue-light protective functions derived from renewable and biodegradable biomass represents a promising strategy for eye protection. In the present study, we introduce a sustainable protecting film by embedding carbon quantum dots derived from Coffea arabica grounds (CAG-CQDs) into a polyurethane (PU) matrix via solvent casting. The CAG-CQDs were synthesized using a carbonization at 300 °C for 2 h followed by ultrasonication for 20 min, and microwave irradiation at 800 W power for 10 min. The PU films were prepared in toluene at 60 °C under continuous stirring, and the CAG-CQDs at different concentrations were incorporated into the hot solution of PU prior to solvent casting at ambient temperature. The CQDs obtained in this study exhibit nanoparticles with an average size of 6.34 ± 0.51 nm, absorb the UV light at λex = 265 nm and capable of emitting a visible light at λem = 445 nm with quantum yield of 16.7%, and a band gap of 4.86 eV. The nanocomposite films show the capability in blocking up to 95% of UV-A, 91% of UV-B and 81% of HEBL radiations, were found to hydrophobic with contact angle of 97.3–107.7 o and low water absorption capacity (2.243–3.242%). The results confirm the potential of polyurethane-CQDs nanocomposite films as protective coatings for electronic displays, including smartphones and tablets.

title: ARDUINO IN TEACHING LABS: A BIBLIOMETRIC ANALYSIS
source: Uluslararası Eğitim Bilim ve Teknoloji Dergisi
summary: Arduino microprocessors are increasingly used in teaching laboratories as a technology that attracts attention with its superior features and ease of use. In this study, it is aimed to carry out a bibliometric analysis to examine the studie
content: Arduino microprocessors are increasingly used in teaching laboratories as a technology that attracts attention with its superior features and ease of use. In this study, it is aimed to carry out a bibliometric analysis to examine the studies using Arduino in teaching laboratories and to assist researchers by predicting the direction of future studies.This study used bibliometric and content analysis. By scanning the WoS and Scopus databases 404 studies were reached and according to various exclusion criteria 215 of them were included in this study. Biblioshiny software was used for analysis, and the studies were also examined with content analysis based on technology-based learning. It is found that Arduino in Teaching Lab. (ATL) research has a high growth rate and the publications in this field mostly have two or more authors, the country with the most publications is the USA. In the studies, it was seen that the majority of the studies aimed at developing the laboratory setups/devices/equipment available on the market at a lower cost, and the majority of studies were carried out in the engineering laboratory with university students. It can be concluded that the use of Arduino in science laboratories is important both in terms of eliminating concerns about laboratory costs and creating opportunities in the learning process. This study focuses on the use of technologies like Arduino in education. The findings presented in this study can be considered as guiding principles for future research.

title: Climate Change Exposure and the Discipline of Capital Structure: Evidence From Managerial Leverage Distortion
summary: ABSTRACT This study examines how climate change exposure affects corporate financing behaviour through the lens of managerial leverage distortion (MLD), defined as the absolute deviation of observed leverage from a benchmark implied by firm
content: ABSTRACT This study examines how climate change exposure affects corporate financing behaviour through the lens of managerial leverage distortion (MLD), defined as the absolute deviation of observed leverage from a benchmark implied by firm fundamentals. Using a large panel of the US firms and high‐dimensional fixed‐effects models with firm‐ and year‐fixed effects, the study finds that climate change exposure is associated with significantly lower MLD, indicating more disciplined, fundamentals‐aligned capital structure decisions. The effect is primarily driven by reductions in under‐leverage distortions, consistent with precautionary financial behaviour. The study documents that managerial incentives, business strategy and firm‐level risk conditions moderate this relationship, with weaker effects in high‐incentive and high‐risk environments. Further, the study reveals that higher MLD is associated with poorer firm performance, higher cost of debt and greater investment inefficiency. Overall, the findings suggest that climate risk improves financial discipline by constraining managerial discretion in capital structure decisions.

title: Isolation of oxygen-dependent nicotine- and pseudooxynicotine-metabolizing enzymes
summary: NicA2 is a flavin-bound amine dehydrogenase from Pseudomonas putida S16 that converts nicotine to the pharmacologically inactive N -methylmyosmine. In animal models of nicotine addiction, injection of NicA2 can decrease nicotine-seeking beh
content: NicA2 is a flavin-bound amine dehydrogenase from Pseudomonas putida S16 that converts nicotine to the pharmacologically inactive N -methylmyosmine. In animal models of nicotine addiction, injection of NicA2 can decrease nicotine-seeking behavior 10-fold. Accordingly, NicA2-related enzymes have been investigated as smoking-cessation therapeutics. However, efficient catalysis by NicA2 in Pseudomonas putida relies on electron transfer to CycN, a cytochrome c, and not directly to O 2 . Impractically high amounts of NicA2 are thus necessary to achieve a pharmacological effect in the absence of CycN. Directed evolution has improved the ambient-O 2 value of k cat from 0.007 s -1 to 1 s -1 for NicA2, but further improvements have been challenging. Here, we identify a strain of Peribacillus frigoritolerans NIC8 which encodes two flavin amine oxidoreductases, Ncox and Pnox. In the presence of oxygen, Ncox and Pnox act on nicotine and pseudooxynicotine respectively with apparent kcat values of 7.7 s -1 and 3.9 s -1 . Transient kinetics establishes bimolecular rate constants of 51100 M -1 s -1 and 81000 M -1 s -1 for the half-reactions between Ncox and O 2 and between Pnox and O 2 respectively, consistent with Ncox and Pnox being bona-fide oxidases. Transcriptomics shows enhanced expression of Ncox and Pnox under nicotine-dependent growth as well as supporting the identification of downstream enzymes. Phylogenetic analysis suggests that Ncox and Pnox arose out of repurposing of homologous enzymes found in Bacillus species. The enzymes we describe may be useful for the development of nicotine addiction therapeutics and for bioconversion of nicotine in waste streams.

title: A broad-host-range bacteriophage SLAM_phiVP16 for post-contamination reduction and prophylactic control of multidrug-resistant Vibrio parahaemolyticus infection in brine shrimp model
summary: Vibrio parahaemolyticus is a major seafood-borne pathogen associated with shrimp contamination and aquaculture disease. This study characterized SLAM_phiVP16, a broad-host-range bacteriophage targeting V. parahaemolyticus , and evaluated it
content: Vibrio parahaemolyticus is a major seafood-borne pathogen associated with shrimp contamination and aquaculture disease. This study characterized SLAM_phiVP16, a broad-host-range bacteriophage targeting V. parahaemolyticus , and evaluated its biocontrol potential in shrimp-related application models. Among the 32 isolated phages, SLAM_phiVP16 lysed all tested V. parahaemolyticus strains, including multidrug-resistant strains isolated from human feces, crustaceans, and seawater. SLAM_phiVP16 exhibited a podovirus-like morphology, a short latent period of approximately 10 min, a burst size of approximately 100 PFU per infected cell, and stability under refrigerated conditions and across a pH range of 4-11. Whole-genome analysis revealed no predicted integrase, antibiotic resistance genes, or known virulence-associated genes, and taxonomic analysis classified SLAM_phiVP16 within the genus Maculvirus and the species Vibrio virus H256D1 . In liquid culture, SLAM_phiVP16 suppressed bacterial growth for approximately 6 h and significantly reduced biofilm formation at 48 h even at the lowest tested phage dose ( P < 0.001). In a post-contamination shrimp model, phage treatment maintained an approximately 1.3 log reduction in V. parahaemolyticus counts during refrigerated storage. In a prophylactic brine shrimp ( Artemia salina ) model, SLAM_phiVP16 significantly improved survival compared with the infected group ( P < 0.05) and reduced bacterial burdens in both water and brine shrimp samples. These findings suggest that SLAM_phiVP16 is a promising phage-based candidate for reducing and preventing V. parahaemolyticus contamination in the shrimp industry chain.

title: Biospheric values and green supply chain management: The mediating effects of generative concern and environmental attitude with moderation by generative leadership
summary: Recently, Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) has gained recognition as a strategic response to sustainability challenges, yet its application in the public sector of developing country is limited. To address this gap, the purpose is to in
content: Recently, Green Supply Chain Management (GSCM) has gained recognition as a strategic response to sustainability challenges, yet its application in the public sector of developing country is limited. To address this gap, the purpose is to investigate the direct role of biospheric values on GSCM and indirectly through generative concerns and environmental attitude. Moreover, the study examines the moderating role of generative leadership on these relationships. Based on the natural resource-based view (NRBV) theory, a theoretical framework is developed. A survey approach was adopted to collect 251 responses from employees working in public sector departments in Pakistan Hazara division. The Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) affirmed that biospheric values positively promote GSCM. Moreover, generative concern and environmental attitude play a mediating role between biospheric values and GSCM. Furthermore, generative leadership significantly moderates the relationship between biospheric values and GSCM, generative concerns, and environmental attitude. The study contributes to theory by extending NRBV to public sector sustainability practices and by highlighting generative concern and environmental attitude as critical mediators. It also establishes generative leadership as a key contextual enhancer. Practically, the findings suggest that embedding pro-environmental values and generative leadership can help public organizations to implement waste-reduction, sustainable supply chain and resource-efficiency strategies.

title: A distributed IoT-enabled MCDM framework for dynamic route optimization of dangerous goods transportation
summary: Logistical challenges arise with the transportation of dangerous goods. This research addresses this problem taking into consideration the essential balance between cost, duration and risk, to ensure a safe and efficient transportation in s
content: Logistical challenges arise with the transportation of dangerous goods. This research addresses this problem taking into consideration the essential balance between cost, duration and risk, to ensure a safe and efficient transportation in sustainable transportation systems. The main contribution is to ensure an optimal route selection for both static environmental factors and the inherent uncertainties of dynamic events captured via Internet of Things (IoT) sensor networks that can necessitate real-time re-routing. Current centralized approaches often struggle to provide such robust route evaluations due to latency and data processing bottlenecks in dynamic environments. Therefore, a distributed Multi-Criteria Decision-Making (MCDM) framework is considered to help in evaluating available transportation routes at the network edge and then decide on the optimal one. Several distinct MCDM methodologies are used to identify variations in these potential paths under two ultimate environmental conditions. The static one where transportation conditions are constant and no changes arise and the dynamic one where the probability of disruptive incidents is incorporated based on real-time streaming data from the IoT nodes. In this work, routes are chosen based on TOPSIS method with weights calculated by those different MCDM methods integrated into a distributed architecture. The outcome is then compared with the selected path when using Dijkstra with the same weights. This work aims to compare the outcomes of the MCDM methods used to predict the best route for the transportation of dangerous goods, offering a robust, scalable and efficient tool for optimizing logistics in this critical domain. Each and every method outcome is compared with the outcome of Dijkstra algorithm.

title: Rethinking the school in the Anthropocene as an ecological and democratic third place
summary: This paper examines education in the Anthropocene as a holistic education focusing on the emergence of viable social organizations in the Anthropocene compatible with the sustainability of human life in society. The school is therefore stud
content: This paper examines education in the Anthropocene as a holistic education focusing on the emergence of viable social organizations in the Anthropocene compatible with the sustainability of human life in society. The school is therefore studied as a structural frame for global behavior development, habits of thinking and acting that structure our interactions with the common world. Regarding contemporary political hurdles challenging social transformations toward sustainable societies within democratic representative governance systems, we emphasize the role of participatory democracy as an essential element for enabling maintenance and care of our shared environment. Therefore, based on the work of John Dewey, we theorize school as the place of socialization that shapes the development of collective politico-ethical habits. We take community gardens as an example for the school form, as it allows students to emerge as an active democratic and ecological community around the care of the nature of the garden as a shared environment, within the human and non-human community of life.

title: From debt to trade: How macroeconomic forces shape ecological footprint in Vietnam–Insights from wavelet-based artificial neural network
summary: Against the backdrop of increasing ecological pressure in emerging economies, this study examines how macroeconomic conditions are associated with ecological footprint (EF) in Vietnam. Using annual data from 2000 to 2024, the study employs
content: Against the backdrop of increasing ecological pressure in emerging economies, this study examines how macroeconomic conditions are associated with ecological footprint (EF) in Vietnam. Using annual data from 2000 to 2024, the study employs Random Forest, Wavelet Artificial Neural Network (ANN) regression, and Wavelet-ANN Granger-type predictability analysis to capture nonlinear, horizon-dependent, and directional predictive relationships between EF and five macroeconomic factors: public debt (DEBT), inflation (INF), financial development (FD), trade openness (TRA), and labor force (LF). The findings reveal that the interplay between macroeconomic variables and EF is heterogeneous and vary across horizons. FD and LF are associated with lower EF over medium- and long-run horizons, while TRA and DEBT exhibit mixed and horizon-specific patterns. INF plays a comparatively weak and unstable role. The Wavelet-ANN Granger predictability results further illustrate that statistically significant predictive relationships are limited and horizon-specific. Specifically, TRA and LF emerge as the most persistent predictors of EF, DEBT becomes relevant over medium and long horizons, while FD provides predictive information in the medium horizon. Overall, the results suggest that ecological sustainability in Vietnam is more closely linked to structural macroeconomic conditions than to short-term fluctuations, underscoring the need to integrate environmental objectives into fiscal management, trade policy, financial-sector reform, and labor-market upgrading.
