The findings indicate that key TQM dimensions include leadership support, teaching process management, quality measurement and evaluation, continuous improvement, faculty development and stakeholder orientation. TQM generally contributes to improved teaching quality, faculty performance, organisational effectiveness and stakeholder satisfaction. However, implementation is constrained by insufficient leadership support, limited teacher participation, weak quality culture and inconsistent evaluation practices. Overall, TQM can enhance higher education teaching quality when it is systematically integrated with institutional leadership, teaching processes, faculty development and continuous improvement mechanisms. The findings provide practical implications for educators, university administrators and policymakers.

title: Train and deploy: Expropriation and accumulation in the generative AI economy
summary: The generative AI industry has seen exponential growth over the past 3 years. We attempt to critically analyse its political economy, through a focus on two moments: the training of models, and their deployment downstream. First, we make th
content: The generative AI industry has seen exponential growth over the past 3 years. We attempt to critically analyse its political economy, through a focus on two moments: the training of models, and their deployment downstream. First, we make the case that generative AI presupposes a number of expropriative processes that enable the exploitation of wage labour in the production of models as commodities. Second, we argue that generative AI represents opportunities for capital to subsume and discipline a number of hitherto unstructured labour processes, concentrated in the sphere of circulation rather than the sphere of production, thereby feeding into crisis. Finally, we describe the mechanisms through which societal surplus is redistributed into the AI industry, concluding that the development and deployment of generative AI should be seen as consistent with the imperatives of capitalist planning, rather than as a mutation within them.

title: Profitability Analysis of Pepper (Capsicum Species) Production in Okene Local Government Area, Kogi State, Nigeria
source: RADINKA JOURNAL OF SCIENCE AND SYSTEMATIC LITERATURE REVIEW
summary: This study investigates the economic viability of and challenges faced by pepper farmers in the region. As a globally significant spice crop of immense culinary and economic importance, pepper contributes to nutritional health and accounts
content: This study investigates the economic viability of and challenges faced by pepper farmers in the region. As a globally significant spice crop of immense culinary and economic importance, pepper contributes to nutritional health and accounts for approximately 40% of vegetable consumption in Nigeria, which yielded 762,174 tonnes of green chilies and peppers in 2020. The research aimed to describe the socio-economic characteristics of chili pepper farmers, assess profitability, and identify production constraints within Okene Local Government Area. Employing a multi-stage sampling technique, data were gathered from 99 respondents using structured questionnaires, personal visits, and interviews. Findings reveal that pepper production in Okene LGA is, on average, profitable, yielding a mean Net Farm Income (NFI) of ₦749,303.03, though significant variability exists, with some farmers experiencing losses. Key constraints identified include sole reliance on pepper farming, limited access to formal credit, and a lack of off-farm employment opportunities. Consequently, the study recommends targeted policy interventions—such as accessible microfinance, improved farm inputs, and stronger agricultural extension services—while emphasizing gender-sensitive development and income diversification to enhance rural sustainability and livelihoods.

title: Fit matters - support configurations and sustainability venture survival
summary: The growing urgency of solving worldwide societal and climate change issues through viable business models has intensified research on entrepreneurship support. Despite the expansion of entrepreneurship support, little is known on how diffe
content: The growing urgency of solving worldwide societal and climate change issues through viable business models has intensified research on entrepreneurship support. Despite the expansion of entrepreneurship support, little is known on how different support configurations interact with sustainability venture orientation and founder characteristics to shape survival outcomes. We reposition venture survival as a critical precondition for long-term sustainable impact and introduce a framework for context-sensitive support design that treats venture orientation - distinguishing social from ecological orientation - as a central contextual condition shaping support effectiveness. Addressing the limited attention on heterogeneity and configurational causality in venture survival research, we employ a configurational approach using qualitative comparative analysis (QCA). Based on a sample of 262 Norwegian ventures and interviews with entrepreneurship support organizations, we show that survival is associated with selectively combined and orientation-aligned support bundles, whereas expansive multi-type support configurations are, in some cases, linked to non-survival. Depending on venture orientation (social vs. ecological), education, and support bundles, we identify distinct configurations associated with both survival and failure, revealing causal asymmetry. Our findings highlight the double-edged nature of entrepreneurship support: while targeted configurations aligned with venture orientation appear to sustain problem-solving and persistence, overly extensive support bundles may crowd out agency and diffuse attention. By demonstrating that support effectiveness depends on configurational alignment rather than additive intensity, this study challenges the assumption that more support is inherently beneficial and advances a context-sensitive perspective on sustainability entrepreneurship support design.

title: Mapping Barriers and Enablers to Institutional Lending for Smallholder Farmers: An Integrative Review and Research Agenda
summary: ABSTRACT Millions of smallholder farmers in Asia and Sub‐Saharan Africa have been crowded out of institutional lending. While unclear property rights or illiquid collateral, isolation, the lack of tailored credit products, and agricultural
content: ABSTRACT Millions of smallholder farmers in Asia and Sub‐Saharan Africa have been crowded out of institutional lending. While unclear property rights or illiquid collateral, isolation, the lack of tailored credit products, and agricultural endowment risks hinder their access to credit from formal channels, the extant literature is scant in mapping barriers and enablers to institutional lending for smallholders and presenting them in a unified framework by integrating theoretical perspectives into a conceptual synthesis. We bridge this gap by conducting an integrative review that combines a bibliometric analysis of 848 articles retrieved from the Scopus database, a systematic literature review of 83 articles, and 29 grey literature sources, utilizing an integrated Antecedents‐Decisions‐Outcomes (ADO) and Theory‐Context‐Characteristic‐Method (TCCM) framework. We identify supply‐side and demand‐side antecedents (barriers) that inform farmer borrowing decisions, lenders’ screening and credit appraisal, and the choice of intermediation channel, thereby shaping farmer credit availability and access, farm investment and agricultural yields, and social and environmental outcomes. The theoretical perspectives emerging from the TCCM framework are categorized into the structural, behavioural, and network layers that affect transaction‐cost attributes of institutional lending. We propose future research directions to address the conceptual and empirical gaps to deepen institutional lending to small‐scale farmers.

title: Competitor Crisis: Determinants of Shell Customer Loyalty Through Satisfaction
summary: This study examines the effects of Perceived Quality, Perceived Value, Brand Image, Brand Identification, and Brand Trust on Customer Satisfaction and Brand Loyalty among Shell fuel consumers in the aftermath of the Pertamina fuel adulterat
content: This study examines the effects of Perceived Quality, Perceived Value, Brand Image, Brand Identification, and Brand Trust on Customer Satisfaction and Brand Loyalty among Shell fuel consumers in the aftermath of the Pertamina fuel adulteration crisis. A quantitative approach was employed using data collected through an online survey of 400 respondents, which were analyzed using Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM). The measurement model demonstrated satisfactory reliability and validity, indicating that all constructs met the recommended criteria for indicator reliability, convergent validity, discriminant validity, and internal consistency. The structural model showed that Perceived Quality, Perceived Value, Brand Identification, Brand Trust, and Brand Image each had positive and significant effects on both Customer Satisfaction and Brand Loyalty. Furthermore, Customer Satisfaction was found to positively and significantly influence Brand Loyalty, confirming its mediating role in strengthening customer loyalty. The model exhibited moderate explanatory power, with R² values of 0.624 for Customer Satisfaction and 0.582 for Brand Loyalty. These findings highlight that both functional and psychological brand-related factors contribute to customer satisfaction and long-term loyalty, while extending the brand loyalty literature by demonstrating how a competitor crisis can create opportunities for strengthening customer relationships through enhanced perceptions of quality, value, trust, identification, and brand image

title: VeriX-Anon: A multi-layered framework for mathematically verifiable outsourced target-driven data anonymization
summary: Organisations increasingly outsource privacy-sensitive data transformations to cloud providers, yet no practical mechanism lets the data owner verify that the contracted algorithm was faithfully executed. VeriX-Anon is a multi-layered verif
content: Organisations increasingly outsource privacy-sensitive data transformations to cloud providers, yet no practical mechanism lets the data owner verify that the contracted algorithm was faithfully executed. VeriX-Anon is a multi-layered verification framework for outsourced Target-Driven k-anonymization combining three orthogonal mechanisms: deterministic verification via Merkle-style hashing of an Authenticated Decision Tree, probabilistic verification via Boundary Sentinels and exact-duplicate Twins with cryptographic identifiers, and utility-based verification via Explainable AI fingerprinting that compares SHAP value distributions before and after anonymization using the Wasserstein distance. Across seven cross-domain datasets and four cloud profiles (28 scenarios), against Lazy (drops records), Dumb (fake hash), and Approximate (valid hash) adversaries, VeriX-Anon detects 25 of 28 deviations under a fixed threshold and 27 of 28 once the threshold is calibrated per dataset, with no false alarms. No single layer achieved this alone. The XAI layer was the only mechanism that caught the Approximate adversary, succeeding on six of seven datasets and missing only a high-dimensional case where honest generalization shifts SHAP as much as the attack. Target-Driven anonymization preserved significantly more utility than blind splitting, with mean F1 gaps of ＋0.058 to ＋0.362 and Wilcoxon 𝑝 ≤ 0 . 0 0 1 on six of seven datasets. Client-side verification completes under one second at one million rows. The threat model covers three empirically evaluated profiles and one theoretical Informed Attacker unable to defeat the cryptographic salt. Sentinel evasion probability ranges from near-zero to 0.82 for the most imbalanced data, which the twin layer offsets in every scenario.

title: The Effect of Communication, Compliance, and Work Discipline on Performance: Moderating Role of Work Ethic
summary: The performance of pilotage services is commonly assessed based on systematic service-time indicators. However, achieving the prescribed service time does not necessarily indicate the absence of operational issues related to pilot work beha
content: The performance of pilotage services is commonly assessed based on systematic service-time indicators. However, achieving the prescribed service time does not necessarily indicate the absence of operational issues related to pilot work behaviour. The present study complements the existing literature by extending the assessment to behavioural factors, including communication, compliance, and work discipline. Furthermore, work ethic is believed to moderate the relationship between these work behaviour factors and performance. Therefore, this study aims to examine the effects of communication, compliance, work discipline, and work ethic on pilot performance, as well as the moderating role of work ethic in these relationships. Pilot performance is assessed using external perceptions, responses from 177 masters of vessels collected through an online questionnaire. This study employs a quantitative method and utilizes PLS-SEM. The findings of this study indicated that communication and compliance do not significantly affect performance. Meanwhile, work discipline and work ethic significantly affect performance. Furthermore, work ethic does not significantly moderate the effect of communication and compliance on performance but significantly moderates the effect of work discipline on performance.

title: POLLUTION HALO EFFECT IN NIGERIA: FOREIGN DIRECT INVESTMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY IN THE CONTEXT OF ENERGY DEPENDENCE AND INSTITUTIONAL GOVERNANCE
source: Journal of Human Social and Political Science Research
summary: This study examines the dynamic relationship between foreign direct investment (FDI) and environmental quality in Nigeria from 1980 to 2023, with particular attention to the moderating roles of institutional quality and nonrenewable energy
content: This study examines the dynamic relationship between foreign direct investment (FDI) and environmental quality in Nigeria from 1980 to 2023, with particular attention to the moderating roles of institutional quality and nonrenewable energy consumption. Employing a novel Dynamic Autoregressive Distributed Lag (D-ARDL) simulation model, the study investigates both long-run equilibrium relationships and short-run dynamics among the variables. The findings reveal that FDI exerts a negative and statistically significant long-run effect on CO₂ emissions, providing robust empirical support for the pollution-halo hypothesis in the Nigerian context. Nonrenewable energy consumption emerges as the strongest driver of environmental degradation, exhibiting positive effects in both short-run and long-run. Institutional quality demonstrates a direct mitigating influence on emissions, though its moderating effect on FDI's environmental impact remains statistically insignificant. Notably, the long-run interaction terms between FDI and institutional quality, as well as between FDI and nonrenewable energy consumption, are statistically insignificant, suggesting that the environmental benefits of FDI operate directly through technology transfer mechanisms rather than through institutional moderation. The error correction term confirms rapid adjustment speed, with 72-80% of short-run deviations corrected within one period. The study contributes to the ongoing debate between pollution-haven and pollution-halo hypotheses by demonstrating that FDI's environmental benefits in Nigeria operate through direct technology transfer mechanisms. These findings carry significant policy implications for Nigeria's green growth strategy and sustainable development pathways.

title: ANALYSIS AND DESIGN OF A SUSTAINABLE SMART PATCHOULI AGROINDUSTRY DEVELOPMENT SYSTEM
summary: Indonesia makes over 95% of the world's nilam oil, but the country's nilam agroindustry still has problems like low productivity, inconsistent quality, reliance on old-fashioned distillation technologies, and inadequate communication betwee
content: Indonesia makes over 95% of the world's nilam oil, but the country's nilam agroindustry still has problems like low productivity, inconsistent quality, reliance on old-fashioned distillation technologies, and inadequate communication between value chain participants. The issue restricts the supplementary benefits that farmers and local enterprises ought to receive. This paper examines the patchouli agroindustry in Sukabumi Regency and suggests a framework for the creation of a sustainable and intelligent system. This study utilizes value chain analysis to delineate the flow of materials and information, SWOT analysis to evaluate strategic situations, and the Business Model Canvas (BMC) to formulate a cooperative-oriented business model. Surveys as well as interviews, FGDs, and field observations were conducted to collect the information from farmers, cooperatives, distillers and traders. The research results imply that village cooperatives has important strategic role as collectors who can help to enhance quality and increase the farmers bargaining position by cutting their dependence of intermediaries. According to SWOT analysis, this industry is in Quadrant II (SO Strategy), suggesting that there is a need for modernization of the distillation processes, cooperative management should be enhanced and quality standards set in place. The proposed-based BMC contributes to a consistent and traceable supply of “blending-ready” oil in an overlapping feed stock structure and promotes the local SMEs collaboration. This material structure also means that the digital can be constantly used to keep things more sustainable. Keywords: patchouli agroindustry; Value chain; Cooperative model; SWOT analysis; Sustainable development

title: The economic gains from breaking boundaries: Reformulating index insurance zones to maximize lower tail dependence
summary: Index insurance intended to help low-wealth households manage risk is hampered by downside basis risk, meaning that the insured suffers a loss, but the insurance index fails to signal a loss. Existing index insurance contracts use statistic
content: Index insurance intended to help low-wealth households manage risk is hampered by downside basis risk, meaning that the insured suffers a loss, but the insurance index fails to signal a loss. Existing index insurance contracts use statistically ad hoc administrative boundaries to demarcate insurance zones. We develop an algorithm that creates zones that maximize lower tail dependence amongst individual units included in each zone. Breaking boundaries in this way minimizes basis risk. Using data from a satellite-based index insurance program in Kenya, we show that replacing administrative with optimized zones can as much as triple the value of insurance using an expected utility-based metric of insurance quality.
